title.zh: 卷一百六十一 志第一百十四 職官一
title.raw: 卷一百六十一 志第一百十四 職官一 Volume 161 Treatises 114: Offical Posts 1

sentences.zh: 三師 三公 宰執 門下省 中書省 尚書省

translations.literal: Three Masters; Three Dukes; Chief Ministers; Chancellery; Secretariat; Department of State Affairs
translations.idiomatic: The Three Masters; the Three Dukes; the Chief Ministers; the Chancellery; the Secretariat; the Department of State Affairs

sentences.zh: 昔武王克商，史臣紀其成功，有曰：“列爵惟五，分土惟三，建官惟賢，位事惟能。”

translations.literal: In antiquity, when King Wu conquered Shang, the historiographer recorded his success, saying: 'Ranks were distributed in five grades, fiefs in three divisions, offices established for the worthy, and posts filled according to ability.'
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu overthrew the Shang, the court historian recorded the achievement in words that have come down to us: 'Assign ranks in five grades, divide the land in three portions, appoint officials for their merit, and place men in office according to their capacity.'

sentences.zh: 後世曰爵，曰官，曰職，分而任之，其原蓋始乎此。

translations.literal: Later ages speak of rank, of office, and of duty, assigning them separately to bear responsibility — the origin of this practice probably begins here.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages would speak of rank, office, and duty as distinct categories, assigning each its own responsibilities — and the root of that practice surely lies here.

sentences.zh: 然周初之制，已不可考。

translations.literal: Yet the institutions of early Zhou can no longer be reconstructed.
translations.idiomatic: The institutions of early Zhou, however, can no longer be fully recovered.

sentences.zh: 周公作六典，自天官冢宰而下，小大高下，各帥其屬以任其事，未聞建官而不任以事，位事而不命以官者；

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou fashioned the Six Canons; from the Minister of Heaven, the Grand Steward, downward, great and small, high and low, each led subordinates to fulfill their tasks. One never hears of establishing an office without assigning work to it, or filling a post without appointing someone to the corresponding office.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou established the Six Canons: from the Minister of Heaven, the Grand Steward, on down through every grade, high and low, each official led his staff to carry out his duties. There is no record of creating an office without assigning it business, or filling a post without conferring the corresponding title.

sentences.zh: 至於列爵分土，此封建諸侯之制也，亦未聞以爵以土，如後世虛稱以備恩數者也。

translations.literal: As for assigning ranks and distributing fiefs, this was the institution of enfeoffing feudal lords. Nor is there any record of ranks and fiefs being used as empty titles, as in later ages when honorific designations were bestowed merely to pad the rolls of imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: As for distributing ranks and granting fiefs, that was the system of enfeoffing feudal lords — and there is likewise no sign that rank and land were handed out as empty titles, the way later dynasties would bestow honorific names merely to swell the rolls of imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢及魏、晉、南北朝，官制沿革不常，不可殫舉。

translations.literal: Under Qin, Han, Wei, Jin, and the Northern and Southern Dynasties, changes in the official hierarchy were unceasing and cannot be exhaustively listed.
translations.idiomatic: From Qin and Han through Wei, Jin, and the Northern and Southern Dynasties, the official system changed without cease; it cannot be set forth in full.

sentences.zh: 後周復《周禮》六典官稱，而參用秦、漢。

translations.literal: Later Zhou restored the official titles of the Six Canons in the "Rites of Zhou," while also drawing on Qin and Han practice.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou revived the official titles of the Six Canons from the "Rites of Zhou," while also incorporating Qin and Han methods.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝廢《周禮》之制，惟用近代之法。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui abolished the "Rites of Zhou" system and used only the methods of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui discarded the "Rites of Zhou" framework and relied solely on the institutions of recent dynasties.

sentences.zh: 唐承隋制，至天授中，始有試官之格，又有員外之置，尋為檢校、試、攝、判、知之名。

translations.literal: Tang inherited the Sui system. In the Tianhou era provisional appointment regulations first appeared, along with supplemental posts; these soon evolved into the categories inspection and superintendency, provisional, acting, concurrent, and nominal supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Tang took over the Sui system. In the Tianhou period, regulations for provisional appointments appeared, followed by supplemental posts; before long these gave rise to the designations inspection and superintendency, provisional, acting, concurrent, and nominal supervision.

sentences.zh: 其初立法之意未嘗不善，蓋欲以名器事功甄別能否，又使不肖者絕年勞序遷之覬覦。

translations.literal: The original legislative intent was not unworthy: it sought to distinguish competence through titles, offices, and actual achievement, and to cut off the unworthy from coveting promotion by seniority alone.
translations.idiomatic: The original intent behind these laws was not bad at all: titles and offices were meant to be matched to real achievement so that ability could be distinguished, and the unworthy were to be denied any hope of advancing by seniority alone.

sentences.zh: 而世戚勛舊之家，寵之以祿，而不責以猷為。

translations.literal: Yet for families of imperial in-laws, meritorious clans, and old associates, emolument was lavished without demanding responsible counsel or performance.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial in-laws, families of meritorious service, and old associates were showered with stipends but not held to any standard of counsel or action.

sentences.zh: 其居位任事者，不限資格，使得自竭其所長，以為治效。

translations.literal: Those who actually held posts and managed affairs were not restricted by seniority requirements, allowing them to fully apply their strengths for administrative effectiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Those who actually held office and handled affairs were not bound by seniority requirements, so that each could bring his full talents to bear and produce results in governance.

sentences.zh: 且黜陟進退之際，權歸於上，而有司若不得預。

translations.literal: Moreover, at moments of promotion and dismissal, power rested with the throne, and the regular offices seemed to have no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to promotion and dismissal, authority rested entirely with the throne, and the regular offices appeared to have no say at all.

sentences.zh: 殊不知名實混殽，品秩貿亂之弊，亦起於是矣。

translations.literal: Little did they realize that the evils of confused names and realities, and jumbled ranks and grades, arose from this very practice.
translations.idiomatic: They did not see that the confusion of names with realities and the disorder of ranks and grades had their origin in this very system.

sentences.zh: 宋承唐制，抑又甚焉。

translations.literal: Song inherited the Tang system — and intensified its defects even further.
translations.idiomatic: Song took over the Tang system and carried its abuses even further.

sentences.zh: 三師、三公不常置，宰相不專任三省長官，尚書、門下併列於外，又別置中書禁中，是為政事堂，與樞密對掌大政。

translations.literal: The Three Masters and Three Dukes were not regularly appointed; the chancellor was not a dedicated post for heads of the Three Departments. The Department of State Affairs and Chancellery stood side by side outside the palace, while a separate Secretariat was set up within the inner quarters — this was the Hall of Administration, which jointly managed great affairs with the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Masters and Three Dukes were not regularly filled; the chancellor did not serve exclusively as head of one of the Three Departments. The Department of State Affairs and the Chancellery stood together outside the palace, while a separate Secretariat was established within the inner quarters — the Hall of Administration — which shared control of major policy with the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 天下財賦，內庭諸司，中外筦庫，悉隸三司。

translations.literal: All empire revenue, inner-palace offices, and domestic and frontier storehouses fell under the Three Fiscal Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: All revenue under heaven, every inner-palace office, and every storehouse at court and on the frontier came under the Three Fiscal Commissions.

sentences.zh: 中書省但掌冊文、覆奏、考帳；

translations.literal: The Secretariat managed only memorial drafts, review submissions, and personnel records.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat handled only document drafts, review submissions, and personnel records.

sentences.zh: 門下省主乘輿八寶，朝會板位，流外考較，諸司附奏挾名而已。

translations.literal: The Chancellery was chiefly responsible for the imperial carriage and eight regalia, seating arrangements at court assemblies, examinations of sub-clerical staff, and merely endorsing memorials submitted by other offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery was chiefly in charge of the imperial carriage and the eight regalia, seating charts for court assemblies, examinations of sub-clerical staff, and nothing more than attaching its seal to memorials routed from other offices.

sentences.zh: 台、省、寺、監，官無定員，無專職，悉皆出入分涖庶務。

translations.literal: At the Censorate, the Departments, the Directorates, and the Commissions, there were no fixed quotas or specific duties; officials moved in and out to share miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the Censorate, the Departments, the Directorates, and the Commissions, posts had no fixed quotas and no dedicated duties; officials rotated in and out to divide up miscellaneous business among themselves.

sentences.zh: 故三省、六曹、二十四司，類以他官主判，雖有正官，非別敕不治本司事，事之所寄，十亡二三。

translations.literal: Thus the Three Departments, six bureaus, and twenty-four offices were mostly supervised by officials from other posts. Even when there were incumbent officials, without a separate edict they did not administer their own department's affairs — of the business nominally entrusted to them, only two or three tenths remained.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments, six bureaus, and twenty-four offices were for the most part run by officials drawn from other posts. Even when a department had its regular incumbent, he did not handle its own affairs unless specially ordered by edict — of the business nominally assigned to these offices, only two or three tenths actually remained with them.

sentences.zh: 故中書令、侍中、尚書令不預朝政，侍郎、給事不領省職，諫議無言責，起居不記註；

translations.literal: Hence the Secretariat Director, Palace Attendant, and Department Director did not attend to court governance; Vice Directors and Drafting Attendants did not perform their departmental duties; Remonstrance officials had no remonstrance responsibility; and Diaries officials kept no diaries.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Director, Palace Attendant, and Department Director took no part in court governance; Vice Directors and Drafting Attendants did not perform their departmental duties; Remonstrance officials bore no remonstrance responsibility; and Diaries officials recorded nothing.

sentences.zh: 中書常闕舍人，門下罕除堂侍，司諫、正言非特旨供職亦不任諫諍。

translations.literal: The Secretariat often lacked drafting attendants; the Chancellery seldom appointed hall attendants; and remonstrance and advisory officials, unless specially ordered to take up their posts, did not perform remonstrance duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat often had no drafting attendants; the Chancellery rarely appointed hall attendants; and remonstrance and advisory officials, unless specifically ordered to serve, did not perform remonstrance duties.

sentences.zh: 至於僕射、尚書、丞、郎、員外，居其官不知其職者，十常八九。

translations.literal: As for Vice Directors, Directors, Assistant Directors, Section Chiefs, and Supplementary Officials — nine times out of ten those who held the titles did not know what their duties were.
translations.idiomatic: As for Vice Directors, Directors, Assistant Directors, Section Chiefs, and Supplementary Officials, nine times out of ten the men who held these titles did not know what their duties were.

sentences.zh: 其官人受授之別，則有官、有職、有差遣。

translations.literal: The categories by which officials received appointments were three: office, post, and commission.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments fell into three categories: office, post, and commission.

sentences.zh: 官以寓祿秩、敘位著，職以待文學之選，而別為差遣以治內外之事。

translations.literal: Office provided emolument rank and recorded standing; post awaited literary selection; commission was separately assigned to govern internal and external affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Office conferred emolument rank and recorded one's standing; post awaited selection on literary merit; commission was assigned separately to govern affairs at court and in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 其次又有階、有勛、有爵。

translations.literal: Beyond these there were also grades, honors of achievement, and peerage ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these there were also grades, honors of achievement, and peerage titles.

sentences.zh: 故仕人以登臺閣、升禁從為顯宦，而不以官之遲速為榮滯；

translations.literal: Thus officials regarded appointment to the registry halls and advancement to inner-court attendance as distinguished posts, and did not measure honor or stagnation by how quickly one climbed the official ladder.
translations.idiomatic: Officials therefore prized appointment to the registry halls and advancement to inner-court attendance as marks of distinction, and did not measure success or stagnation by how quickly one climbed the official ladder.

sentences.zh: 以差遣要劇為貴途，而不以階、勛、爵邑有無為輕重。

translations.literal: They took important and demanding commissions as the honored path, and did not weigh prestige by whether one held grades, honors, or fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: They regarded important and demanding commissions as the honored path to advancement, and did not measure a man's standing by whether he possessed grades, honors, or fiefs.

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：“寧登瀛，不為卿；

translations.literal: People of the time said: 'Better to ascend to the Immortal Isle than to be a minister.'
translations.idiomatic: A saying of the time ran: 'Better to reach the Immortal Isle than to become a minister.'

sentences.zh: 寧抱槧，不為監。”

translations.literal: Better to carry writing tablets than to be a director.
translations.idiomatic: Better to carry writing tablets than to serve as a director.

sentences.zh: 虛名不足以砥礪天下若此。

translations.literal: Empty titles were insufficient to sharpen the realm to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the extent to which empty titles had ceased to sharpen the ambitions of the realm.

sentences.zh: 外官，則懲五代藩鎮專恣，頗用文臣知州，復設通判以貳之。

translations.literal: For local posts, to check the autocratic power of Five Dynasties military governors, civil officials were widely sent as prefectural administrators, with deputy commissioners re-established to serve as counters.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces, to guard against the autocratic power of the Five Dynasties military governors, civil officials were widely appointed as prefectural administrators, and deputy commissioners were re-established to serve as their seconds.

sentences.zh: 階官未行之先，州縣守令，多帶中朝職事官外補；

translations.literal: Before the rank-grade system was implemented, prefectural and county magistrates mostly held concurrent metropolitan office titles while serving in provincial appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Before the rank-grade system took effect, prefectural and county magistrates mostly held concurrent metropolitan office titles while serving in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 階官既行之後，或帶或否，視是為優劣。

translations.literal: After the rank-grade system was implemented, whether one held such a concurrent title or not was taken as a mark of superior or inferior standing.
translations.idiomatic: After the rank-grade system was in place, whether a magistrate held such a concurrent title or not was taken as a measure of his standing.

sentences.zh: 大凡一品以下，謂之“文武官”；

translations.literal: Generally, from first rank downward were called 'civil and military officials.'
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, officials from first rank downward were called 'civil and military officials.'

sentences.zh: 未常參者，謂之“京官”；

translations.literal: Those who did not attend regular court audience were called 'capital officials.'
translations.idiomatic: Those who did not attend regular court audience were called 'capital officials.'

sentences.zh: 樞密、宣徽、三司使副、學士、諸司而下，謂之“內職”；

translations.literal: From the Bureau of Military Affairs, Bureau of Palace Attendants, deputy commissioners of the Three Fiscal Offices, academicians, and offices beneath them were called 'inner posts.'
translations.idiomatic: From the Bureau of Military Affairs, the Bureau of Palace Attendants, deputy commissioners of the Three Fiscal Offices, academicians, and the offices beneath them were called 'inner posts.'

sentences.zh: 殿前都校以下，謂之“軍職”。

translations.literal: From the Chief Commander of the Hall of Front Guard downward were called 'military posts.'
translations.idiomatic: From the Chief Commander of the Hall of Front Guard downward were called 'military posts.'

sentences.zh: 外官則有親民、釐務二等，而監軍、巡警亦比親民。

translations.literal: Local posts were divided into those governing the people and those handling fiscal affairs, while military supervisors and circuit patrol officers were classed with the people's governors.
translations.idiomatic: Local posts were divided into those governing the people and those handling fiscal affairs; military supervisors and circuit patrol officers were classed with the people's governors.

sentences.zh: 此其概也。

translations.literal: This is the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the general scheme.

sentences.zh: 故自真宗、仁宗以來，議者多以正名為請。

translations.literal: From Emperors Zhenzong and Renzong onward, memorialists frequently pleaded for rectification of names.
translations.idiomatic: From the reigns of Zhenzong and Renzong onward, memorialists repeatedly called for rectifying official titles.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，楊億首言：“文昌會府，有名無實，宜復其舊。”

translations.literal: In the Xianping era, Yang Yi was the first to say: 'The Department of State Affairs, the great assembly of offices, has a name but no substance; its former functions should be restored.'
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era, Yang Yi was the first to argue: 'The Department of State Affairs — the great assembly of offices — exists in name only; its former functions ought to be restored.'

sentences.zh: 既而言者相繼，乞復二十四司之制。

translations.literal: After this, memorialists followed one after another, requesting restoration of the twenty-four offices.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists then followed in succession, calling for the restoration of the twenty-four offices.

sentences.zh: 至和中，吳育亦言：“尚書省，天下之大有司，而廢為閑所，當漸復之。”

translations.literal: In the Zhihe era, Wu Yu also said: 'The Department of State Affairs is the great office of the realm, yet it has been reduced to an idle institution; it should gradually be restored.'
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhihe era, Wu Yu likewise argued: 'The Department of State Affairs is the great governing office of the realm, yet it has been reduced to an idle institution — it should be gradually restored.'

sentences.zh: 然朝論異同，未遑釐正。

translations.literal: Yet court opinion was divided, and there was no leisure to rectify the system.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion remained divided, however, and there was no opportunity to put matters right.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，慨然欲更其制。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, he resolved to reform the system.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong came to the throne, he resolved with deep feeling to reform the system.

sentences.zh: 熙寧末，始命館閣校《唐六典》。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xining era, the Hanlin Academy and Institute were ordered to collate the "Tang Six Codes."
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Xining era, the academy and institute were ordered to collate the "Tang Six Codes."

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，以摹本賜群臣，乃置局中書，命翰林學士張璪等詳定。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng, rubbings were bestowed on the ministers; a bureau was then established within the Secretariat, and Hanlin Academician Zhang Can and others were ordered to review and fix the details.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfeng, rubbings were distributed to the ministers; a review bureau was set up within the Secretariat, and Hanlin Academician Zhang Can and others were charged with working out the details.

sentences.zh: 八月，下詔肇新官制，省、台、寺、監領空名者一切罷去，而易之以階。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict inaugurated the new official system: all empty titles at the Departments, Censorate, Directorates, and Commissions were abolished and replaced with grades.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict inaugurated the new official system: every empty title at the Departments, Censorate, Directorates, and Commissions was abolished and replaced with rank grades.

sentences.zh: 九月，詳定所上《寄祿格》。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the review bureau submitted the "Salary Schedule for Titular Offices."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the review bureau submitted the "Salary Schedule for Titular Offices."

sentences.zh: 會明堂禮成，近臣遷秩即用新制，而省、台、寺、監之官，各還所職矣。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall rite was completed, close ministers were promoted under the new system, and officials of the Departments, Censorate, Directorates, and Commissions each returned to their proper duties.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall rite was completed, close ministers were promoted under the new system, and officials of the Departments, Censorate, Directorates, and Commissions each returned to their proper duties.

sentences.zh: 五年，省、台、寺、監法成。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the regulations for the Departments, Censorate, Directorates, and Commissions were completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the regulations governing the Departments, Censorate, Directorates, and Commissions were completed.

sentences.zh: 六年，尚書新省成，帝親臨幸，召六曹長貳以下，詢以職事，因誡敕焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the new Department of State Affairs building was completed; the emperor visited in person, summoned the heads and deputies of the six bureaus and those below them, inquired into their duties, and issued admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the new Department of State Affairs building was completed. The emperor visited in person, summoned the chiefs and deputies of the six bureaus and their subordinates, questioned them about their duties, and issued admonitions.

sentences.zh: 初，新階尚少，而轉行者易以混雜。

translations.literal: At first the new grades were still few, and transfers among them were easily confused.
translations.idiomatic: At first the new grades were still few in number, and transfers among them were easily confused.

sentences.zh: 及元祐初，於朝議大夫六階以上始分左右。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era, left and right distinctions were first introduced for the six grades from Court Gentleman for Discussion of Governance upward.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era, left and right distinctions were first introduced for the six grades from Court Gentleman for Discussion of Governance upward.

sentences.zh: 既又以流品無別，乃詔寄祿官悉分左右，詞人為左，餘人為右。

translations.literal: Then, because there was no distinction among ranks, an edict ordered that all titular offices be divided into left and right — literary officials on the left, all others on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Because there was still no distinction among ranks, an edict then ordered that all titular offices be divided into left and right: literary officials on the left, all others on the right.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中罷之。

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng era this was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: This arrangement was abolished during the Shaosheng era.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初，以議者有請，自承直至將仕郎，凡換選人七階。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongning era, at memorialists' request, seven grades were exchanged for examination candidates, from Gentleman for Fostering Integrity down to Gentleman for Initial Merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongning era, at memorialists' request, seven grades were established for examination candidates, from Gentleman for Fostering Integrity down to Gentleman for Initial Merit.

sentences.zh: 大觀初，又增宣奉至奉直大夫四階。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daguan era, four more grades were added, from Gentleman for Proclaiming Service to Grandee for Direct Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daguan era, four more grades were added, from Gentleman for Proclaiming Service to Grandee for Direct Integrity.

sentences.zh: 政和末，自從政至迪功郎，又改選人三階，於是文階始備。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenghe era, three more grades for examination candidates were revised, from Gentleman for Following Governance to Gentleman for Advancing Merit — and with this the civil grades were complete.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenghe era, three more grades for examination candidates were revised, from Gentleman for Following Governance to Gentleman for Advancing Merit — and with that the civil grades were complete.

sentences.zh: 而武階亦詔易以新名：正使為大夫，副使為郎，而橫班十二階使、副亦然。

translations.literal: Military grades were likewise ordered renamed: chief commissioners became grandees, deputy commissioners became gentlemen, and the same applied to the twelve lateral grades of commissioners and deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Military grades were likewise ordered renamed: chief commissioners became grandees, deputy commissioners became gentlemen, and the same applied to the twelve lateral grades of commissioners and deputies.

sentences.zh: 故有郎居大夫之上者。

translations.literal: Hence there were cases in which a gentleman ranked above a grandee.
translations.idiomatic: The result was that a gentleman could rank above a grandee.

sentences.zh: 繼以新名未具，增置宣正履正大夫、郎凡十階，通為橫班，而文武官制益加詳矣。

translations.literal: Then, because the new names were not yet complete, ten more grades were added — Grandees and Gentlemen for Proclaiming Integrity and Upholding Integrity — forming the lateral series, and the civil and military systems became still more detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Because the new names were not yet complete, ten more grades were then added — Grandees and Gentlemen for Proclaiming Integrity and Upholding Integrity — forming the lateral series, and the civil and military systems became still more detailed.

sentences.zh: 大抵自元祐以後，漸更元豐之制：二府不分班奏事，樞密加置簽書，戶部則不令右曹專典常平而總於其長，起居郎、舍人則通記起居而不分言動，館職則增置校勘黃本。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, from Yuanyou onward the Yuanfeng system was gradually altered: the Two Departments no longer reported separately in court audience; a drafting secretary was added to the Bureau of Military Affairs; the Ministry of Revenue no longer allowed its right bureau alone to manage the Ever-Normal Granary but consolidated authority in its chief; Diaries Attendants and Drafting Attendants recorded attendance jointly without separating words from actions; and academy posts gained additional collation and yellow-copy review duties.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, from Yuanyou onward the Yuanfeng system was gradually altered: the Two Departments no longer reported separately in court audience; a drafting secretary was added to the Bureau of Military Affairs; the Ministry of Revenue no longer allowed its right bureau alone to manage the Ever-Normal Granary but consolidated authority in its chief; Diaries Attendants and Drafting Attendants recorded attendance jointly without separating words from actions; and academy posts gained additional collation and yellow-copy review duties.

sentences.zh: 凡此，皆與元豐稍異也。

translations.literal: All of these differed slightly from the Yuanfeng system.
translations.idiomatic: All of these differed slightly from the Yuanfeng arrangements.

sentences.zh: 其後蔡京當國，率意自用。

translations.literal: Later, when Cai Jing held power, he acted entirely according to his own will.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Cai Jing dominated the government, he acted entirely on his own judgment.

sentences.zh: 然動以繼志為言，首更開封守臣為尹、牧，由是府分六曹，縣分六案。

translations.literal: Yet he constantly spoke of carrying on his predecessor's intent: he first changed the title of the Kaifeng administrator to Intendant and Pastoral Lord, and on this basis divided the prefecture into six bureaus and the counties into six sections.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he constantly spoke of carrying on his predecessor's intent: he first changed the title of the Kaifeng administrator to Intendant and Pastoral Lord, and on this basis divided the prefecture into six bureaus and the counties into six sections.

sentences.zh: 又內侍省職，悉仿機廷之號。

translations.literal: The posts of the Inner Service Directorate were also all modeled on the titles of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The posts of the Inner Service Directorate were likewise modeled on the titles of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 已而修六尚局，建三衛，即又更兩省之長為左輔、右弼，易端揆之稱為太宰、少宰。

translations.literal: Then he reorganized the Six Directorates Bureau, established the Three Guards, and further changed the heads of the Two Departments to Left and Right Assistants, replacing the title Chief Counselor with Grand Steward and Junior Steward.
translations.idiomatic: He then reorganized the Six Directorates Bureau, established the Three Guards, and further changed the heads of the Two Departments to Left and Right Assistants, replacing the title Chief Counselor with Grand Steward and Junior Steward.

sentences.zh: 是時員既濫冗，名且紊雜。

translations.literal: At this time posts were both excessive and redundant, and titles were confused and jumbled.
translations.idiomatic: By this time posts had proliferated beyond all reason, and titles had become a tangled mess.

sentences.zh: 甚者走馬承受升擁使華；

translations.literal: In extreme cases, mounted dispatch receivers were promoted to hold the splendor of commissioner titles.
translations.idiomatic: In extreme cases, mounted dispatch receivers were promoted to hold the splendor of commissioner titles.

sentences.zh: 黃冠道流，亦濫朝品。

translations.literal: Daoist priests in yellow caps also indiscriminately received court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist priests in yellow caps also received court ranks indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 元豐之制，至此大壞。

translations.literal: The Yuanfeng system was thoroughly ruined by this point.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanfeng system was thoroughly ruined by this point.

sentences.zh: 及宣和末，王黼用事，方且追咎元祐紛更，乃請設局，以修《官制格目》為正名，亦何補矣。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xuanhe era, when Wang Fu held power, he began by blaming the Yuanyou changes; he then requested the establishment of a bureau to compile the "Official System Compendium" for rectifying names — but what good did that do?
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xuanhe era, when Wang Fu held power, he began by blaming the Yuanyou changes; he then requested the establishment of a bureau to compile the "Official System Compendium" for rectifying names — but what good did that do?

sentences.zh: 建炎中興，參酌潤色，因呂頤浩之請，左、右僕射並同中書門下平章事，兩省侍郎改為參知政事，三省之政合乎一。

translations.literal: At the Jianyan restoration, arrangements were adjusted and refined: at Lü Yihao's request, the Left and Right Vice Directors were both made Grand Counselors of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Vice Directors of the Two Departments were changed to Vice Grand Counselors, unifying the governance of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jianyan restoration, arrangements were adjusted and refined: at Lü Yihao's request, the Left and Right Vice Directors were both made Grand Counselors of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Vice Directors of the Two Departments were changed to Vice Grand Counselors, unifying the governance of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 乾道八年，又改左、右僕射為左、右丞相，刪去三省長官虛稱，道揆之名遂定。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qiandao, the Left and Right Vice Directors were further changed to Left and Right Chancellors, empty titles for heads of the Three Departments were removed, and the name for the chief minister was settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Qiandao, the Left and Right Vice Directors were further changed to Left and Right Chancellors, empty titles for heads of the Three Departments were removed, and the name for the chief minister was settled.

sentences.zh: 然維時多艱，政尚權宜。

translations.literal: Yet the times were difficult, and governance favored expedient measures.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the times were difficult, and governance favored expedient measures.

sentences.zh: 御營置使，國用置使，修政局置提舉，軍馬置都督，並以宰相兼之。

translations.literal: Commissioners were established for the Imperial Camp, for State Revenue, for the Bureau of Policy Reform, and for Military Affairs — all held concurrently by the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners were established for the Imperial Camp, for State Revenue, for the Bureau of Policy Reform, and for Military Affairs — all held concurrently by the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 總制司理財，同都督、督視理兵，並以執政兼之。

translations.literal: The General Control Office managed finances; the Co-Commissioner and Inspector-General managed troops — all held concurrently by grand counselors.
translations.idiomatic: The General Control Office managed finances; the Co-Commissioner and Inspector-General managed troops — all held concurrently by grand counselors.

sentences.zh: 因事創名，殊非經久。

translations.literal: Titles were created ad hoc for particular tasks — nothing designed to last.
translations.idiomatic: Titles were created ad hoc for particular tasks — nothing designed to last.

sentences.zh: 惟樞密本兵，與中書對掌機務，號東、西二府，命宰相兼知院事。

translations.literal: Only the Bureau of Military Affairs, which controlled the military, shared management of state secrets with the Secretariat — they were called the Eastern and Western Departments — and the chancellor was ordered to serve concurrently as Director of the Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Bureau of Military Affairs, which controlled the military, shared management of state secrets with the Secretariat — they were called the Eastern and Western Departments — and the chancellor was ordered to serve concurrently as Director of the Bureau.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，實用慶歷故典。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyan, the old Qingli precedent was actually put into use.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianyan, the old Qingli precedent was actually put into use.

sentences.zh: 其後，兵興則兼樞密使，兵罷則免；

translations.literal: Thereafter, when war arose the chancellor concurrently held the post of Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; when war ended he was relieved of it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, when war arose the chancellor concurrently held the post of Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; when war ended he was relieved of it.

sentences.zh: 至開禧初，始以宰臣兼樞密為永制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaixi era, the chancellor's concurrent service as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs first became a permanent institution.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaixi era, the chancellor's concurrent service as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs first became a permanent institution.

sentences.zh: 當多事時，諸部或長貳不並置，或並郎曹使相兼之，惟吏部、戶部不省不並。

translations.literal: In times of many affairs, some ministries might not have both chief and deputy in place at once, or section chiefs and commissioners might hold concurrent posts — only the Ministry of Personnel and Ministry of Revenue were neither reduced nor combined.
translations.idiomatic: In times of crisis, some ministries might not have both chief and deputy in place at once, or section chiefs and commissioners might hold concurrent posts — only the Ministry of Personnel and Ministry of Revenue were neither reduced nor combined.

sentences.zh: 兵休稍稍增置。

translations.literal: When warfare subsided, posts were gradually increased again.
translations.idiomatic: When warfare subsided, posts were gradually restored.

sentences.zh: 其後，詔非曾任監司、守臣，不除郎官，著為令。

translations.literal: Later an edict ordered that no one who had not previously served as a circuit intendant or prefectural administrator could be appointed a section chief — and this was established as a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict ordered that no one who had not previously served as a circuit intendant or prefectural administrator could be appointed a section chief — and this was established as a permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 又增館閣員，廣環衛官。

translations.literal: Academy posts were increased and palace guard offices expanded.
translations.idiomatic: Academy posts were increased and palace guard offices expanded.

sentences.zh: 然紹興務行元祐故事，以“左右”二字分別流品，其後，以人言省去，寧清濁相涵，無絕人遷善之路。

translations.literal: Yet in the Shaoxing era the Yuanyou precedent was followed: the characters 'left' and 'right' were used to distinguish ranks. Later, at people's urging, this was removed — better to let the pure and impure mingle than to cut off all paths by which men might improve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the Shaoxing era the Yuanyou precedent was followed: the characters 'left' and 'right' were used to distinguish ranks. Later, at people's urging, this was removed — better to let the pure and impure mingle than to cut off all paths by which men might improve themselves.

sentences.zh: 橫班以郎居大夫之上，既釐而正之矣，而介胄之士與縉紳同稱，寧名號未正，毋示人以好武之機。

translations.literal: In the lateral series, gentlemen had ranked above grandees — this had already been corrected — yet armored warriors shared titles with silk-gowned officials; better to leave the names unsettled than to show the world an inclination toward militarism.
translations.idiomatic: In the lateral series, gentlemen had ranked above grandees — this had already been corrected — yet armored warriors shared titles with silk-gowned officials; better to leave the names unsettled than to show the world an inclination toward militarism.

sentences.zh: 陳傅良欲定史官遷次之序，眾論韙之，而未及行。

translations.literal: Chen Fuliang wished to fix the order of promotion for historiography officials; public opinion approved, but it was never carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Fuliang wished to fix the order of promotion for historiography officials; public opinion approved, but it was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 洪邁欲改三衙軍官稱謂，當時嘉之，卒未暇講。

translations.literal: Hong Mai wished to change the titles of the Three Guards military officers; his contemporaries praised the idea, but in the end there was no leisure to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Mai wished to change the titles of the Three Guards military officers; his contemporaries praised the idea, but in the end there was no leisure to discuss it.

sentences.zh: 考古之制，量今之宜，蓋自元祐以逮政和，已未嘗拘乎元豐之舊。

translations.literal: Examining ancient institutions and weighing present needs — from Yuanyou through Zhenghe, the Yuanfeng old system had already ceased to be binding.
translations.idiomatic: Examining ancient institutions and weighing present needs — from Yuanyou through Zhenghe, the Yuanfeng old system had already ceased to be binding.

sentences.zh: 中興若稽成憲，二者並行而不悖。

translations.literal: At the restoration, both were followed in accordance with established statutes, proceeding in parallel without conflict.
translations.idiomatic: At the restoration, both were followed in accordance with established statutes, proceeding in parallel without conflict.

sentences.zh: 故凡大而分政任事之臣，微而筦庫監局之官，沿襲不革者，皆先後所同便也。

translations.literal: Thus whether great ministers who divided governance and bore responsibility, or minor officials who managed storehouses and commissions — those whose titles were retained unchanged were all arrangements found convenient at different times.
translations.idiomatic: Thus whether great ministers who divided governance and bore responsibility, or minor officials who managed storehouses and commissions — those whose titles were retained unchanged were all arrangements found convenient at different times.

sentences.zh: 或始創而終罷，或欲革而猶因，則有各當其可者焉。

translations.literal: Some were first created and later abolished; some were desired to be reformed yet retained — in each case there was what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Some were first created and later abolished; some were desired to be reformed yet retained — in each case there was what was fitting.

sentences.zh: 類而書之，先後互見，作《職官志》。

translations.literal: Arranging these by category and setting them down in writing, with earlier and later arrangements appearing side by side, the "Treatise on Official Posts" was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Arranging these by category and setting them down in writing, with earlier and later arrangements appearing side by side, the "Treatise on Official Posts" was composed.

sentences.zh: 以至廩給、傔 從，雖微必錄，並從舊述雲。

translations.literal: Even stipends and attendants — however minor — are recorded without omission, all following the earlier account.
translations.idiomatic: Even stipends and attendants — however minor — are recorded without omission, all following the earlier account.

sentences.zh: 三師 三公宋承唐制，以太師、太傅、太保為三師，太尉、司徒、司空為三公，為宰相、親王使相加官，其特拜者不預政事，皆赴上於尚書省。

translations.literal: Three Masters and Three Dukes: Song inherited Tang institutions, taking Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Mentor as the Three Masters, and Grand Commandant, Minister over the Masses, and Minister of Works as the Three Dukes; these served as additional titles for chancellors, imperial princes, and commissioner-chancellors; those specially appointed did not participate in government affairs, and all presented themselves at court at the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Following Tang precedent, the Song designated Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Mentor as the Three Masters, and Grand Commandant, Minister over the Masses, and Minister of Works as the Three Dukes. These ranks were supplementary honors for chancellors, imperial princes, and military commissioners holding concurrent chancellor titles. Officials specially elevated to them took no part in actual governance, though all were still required to attend court at the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 凡除授，則自司徒遷太保，自太傅遷太尉，檢校官亦如之。

translations.literal: For all appointments and transfers, one moved from Minister over the Masses to Grand Mentor, and from Grand Tutor to Grand Commandant; provisional (jianjiao) appointments followed the same pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever these offices were filled or transferred, the usual ladder ran from Minister over the Masses to Grand Mentor, and from Grand Tutor to Grand Commandant; acting appointees advanced along the same sequence.

sentences.zh: 太尉舊在三師下，由唐至宋加重，遂以太尉居太傅之上。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant formerly ranked below the Three Masters; from Tang into Song its weight increased, so Grand Commandant came to stand above Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Historically the Grand Commandant had ranked beneath the Three Masters, but from Tang into Song its prestige rose until it was placed above the Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 若宰臣官至僕射致仕者，以在位久近，或已任司空、司徒，則拜太尉、太傅等官。

translations.literal: When chancellors reached Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and retired, depending on length of service, or if they already held Minister of Works or Minister over the Masses, they were appointed Grand Commandant, Grand Tutor, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors who retired after reaching the rank of Vice Director were sometimes awarded Grand Commandant or Grand Tutor, depending on how long they had served—or on whether they already held Minister of Works or Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 若太師則為異數，自趙普以開國元勛，文彥博以累朝耆德，方特拜焉。

translations.literal: As for Grand Preceptor, it was an exceptional rank; only Zhao Pu, as a founding merit, and Wen Yanbo, as accumulated virtue across reigns, received special appointment thereto.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor was a mark of exceptional favor; only Zhao Pu, honored as a founding hero, and Wen Yanbo, revered for virtue across several reigns, were specially appointed to it.

sentences.zh: 雖太傅王旦、司徒呂夷簡各任宰相二十年，止以太尉致仕。

translations.literal: Although Grand Tutor Wang Dan and Minister over the Masses Lü Yijian each served as chancellor for twenty years, they retired only as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Even Wang Dan, eventually Grand Tutor, and Lü Yijian, Minister over the Masses, each held the chancellorship for twenty years yet retired with no higher honor than Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，富弼除守司空兼侍中、平章事，辭司空、侍中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining, Fu Bi was appointed Acting Minister of Works concurrent with Palace Attendant and Grand Councilor, but declined Minister of Works and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 2 (1069), Fu Bi was offered Acting Minister of Works along with Palace Attendant and Grand Councilor; he declined the first two titles.

sentences.zh: 三年，曾公亮除守司空、檢校太師兼侍中，以兩朝定策之功辭相位也。

translations.literal: In the third year, Zeng Gongliang was appointed Acting Minister of Works and Acting Grand Preceptor concurrent with Palace Attendant; citing his merit in securing the succession across two reigns, he resigned the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, Zeng Gongliang was made Acting Minister of Works and Acting Grand Preceptor with concurrent Palace Attendant; he stepped down from the chancellorship, citing his service in settling the succession across two reigns.

sentences.zh: 六年，文彥博除守司徒兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Wen Yanbo was appointed Acting Minister over the Masses concurrent with Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, Wen Yanbo received the title of Acting Minister over the Masses with concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 九年，彥博除守太保兼侍中，辭太保。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Yanbo was appointed Acting Grand Mentor concurrent with Palace Attendant, but declined Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9, Yanbo was made Acting Grand Mentor with concurrent Palace Attendant but declined the Grand Mentor title.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，以曹佾檢校太師、守司徒兼中書令。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng, Cao Yi was appointed Acting Grand Preceptor, Acting Minister over the Masses, and concurrent Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfeng (1080), Cao Yi was given Acting Grand Preceptor and Acting Minister over the Masses, with concurrent Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔檢校官除三公、三師外並罷。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict abolished all provisional appointments except those to the Three Dukes and Three Masters.
translations.idiomatic: That September, an edict eliminated every acting appointment except those to the Three Dukes and Three Masters.

sentences.zh: 又以文彥博落兼侍中，除守太尉，富弼守司徒，皆錄定策之功也。

translations.literal: Further, Wen Yanbo was stripped of his concurrent Palace Attendant title and appointed Acting Grand Commandant; Fu Bi was made Acting Minister over the Masses—both in recognition of their merit in settling the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo lost his concurrent Palace Attendant rank and was appointed Acting Grand Commandant; Fu Bi received Acting Minister over the Masses—both honors recognizing their role in securing the imperial succession.

sentences.zh: 六年，彥博守太師致仕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Yanbo retired as Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, Yanbo retired from office while holding the title of Acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 八年，王安石守司空，曹佾守太保。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Wang Anshi held Acting Minister of Works, and Cao Yi held Acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, Wang Anshi served as Acting Minister of Works and Cao Yi as Acting Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，文彥博落致仕，太師、平章軍國重事，呂公著守司空、同平章軍國重事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, Wen Yanbo was recalled from retirement as Grand Preceptor with authority over state and military affairs; Lü Gongzhuo was made Acting Minister of Works with concurrent authority over state and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 1 (1086), Wen Yanbo was brought back from retirement as Grand Preceptor with charge over state and military affairs; Lü Gongzhuo became Acting Minister of Works with the same concurrent authority.

sentences.zh: 崇寧三年，蔡京授司空，行尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongning, Cai Jing was granted Minister of Works and served as Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 3 (1104), Cai Jing received Minister of Works and served as Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，京為太尉；

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan, Jing became Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan 1, Jing was elevated to Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 二年，為太師。

translations.literal: In the second year, he became Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，京落致仕，依前太師，三日一至都堂治事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, Jing was released from retirement, retaining his former Grand Preceptor title, with orders to attend the chief secretariat once every three days to conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 2 (1112), Jing was recalled from retirement as Grand Preceptor and required to appear at the chief secretariat once every three days to handle business.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔： “以太師、太傅、太保，古三公之官，今為三師，古無此稱，合依三代為三公，為真相之任。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict stated: "Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Mentor were the ancient Three Dukes; today they are called the Three Masters—a title unknown in antiquity. They should be restored as the Three Dukes of the Three Dynasties, bearing the duties of true chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: That September an edict declared: "Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Mentor were the Three Dukes of old; calling them the Three Masters is a later usage with no ancient warrant. They should again be the Three Dukes of the Three Dynasties, charged with the responsibilities of genuine chancellors.

sentences.zh: 司徒、司空，周六卿之官，太尉，秦主兵之任，皆非三公，並宜罷之。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses and Minister of Works were offices of the Zhou Six Ministers; Grand Commandant was the Qin post for commanding troops—none were truly Three Dukes, and all should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: "Minister over the Masses and Minister of Works belonged to the Zhou Six Ministers, and Grand Commandant was originally a Qin military command—none properly constituted the Three Dukes, and all were to be abolished.

sentences.zh: 仍考周制，立三孤少師、少傅、少保，亦稱三少，為三次相之任。”

translations.literal: Still following Zhou institutions, Junior Preceptor, Junior Tutor, and Junior Mentor—also called the Three Juniors—were to be established as posts for secondary chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing again on Zhou practice, Junior Preceptor, Junior Tutor, and Junior Mentor—the Three Juniors—were established as secondary chancellor posts.

sentences.zh: 至是，京始以三公任真相。

translations.literal: At this point Jing first held a Three Duke rank as true chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Jing first occupy a Three Duke title as a genuine chancellor.

sentences.zh: 三公自國初以來，未嘗備官。

translations.literal: Since the founding of the dynasty, the Three Dukes had never been fully staffed.
translations.idiomatic: From the dynasty's founding, the Three Duke posts had never once been filled to capacity.

sentences.zh: 獨宣和末，三公至十八人，三少不計也。

translations.literal: Only at the end of the Xuanhe reign did Three Dukes reach eighteen men, not counting the Three Juniors.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the closing years of Xuanhe did the Three Dukes swell to eighteen holders, the Three Juniors not included in that count.

sentences.zh: 太師三人：蔡京、童貫、鄭紳；

translations.literal: Three Grand Preceptors: Cai Jing, Tong Guan, and Zheng Shen.
translations.idiomatic: The three Grand Preceptors were Cai Jing, Tong Guan, and Zheng Shen.

sentences.zh: 太傅四人：王黼、燕王俁、越王偲、鄆王楷；

translations.literal: Four Grand Tutors: Wang Fu, the Prince of Yan You, the Prince of Yue Cun, and the Prince of Yun Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Four men held Grand Tutor: Wang Fu, Prince of Yan You, Prince of Yue Cun, and Prince of Yun Kai.

sentences.zh: 太保十一人：蔡攸、肅王樞至儀王。

translations.literal: Eleven Grand Mentors: Cai You, the Prince Su Shu, through the Prince of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven Grand Mentors ranged from Cai You and Prince Su Shu down through the Prince of Yi.

sentences.zh: 渡江後，秦檜為太師，張俊、韓世忠為太傅，劉光世為太保。

translations.literal: After the crossing south, Qin Hui became Grand Preceptor; Zhang Jun and Han Shizhong became Grand Tutors; Liu Guangshi became Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Following the flight south of the Yangzi, Qin Hui was made Grand Preceptor, Zhang Jun and Han Shizhong Grand Tutors, and Liu Guangshi Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 乾道初，楊沂中、吳璘併為太傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiandao, Yang Yizhong and Wu Lin both became Grand Tutors.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qiandao era, Yang Yizhong and Wu Lin were both appointed Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 紹熙初，史浩為太師，嗣秀王為太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxi, Shi Hao became Grand Preceptor, and the heir Prince of Xiu became Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Shaoxi, Shi Hao received Grand Preceptor and the heir Prince of Xiu received Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 自紹熙後，三公未嘗備官。

translations.literal: After Shaoxi, the Three Dukes were never again fully staffed.
translations.idiomatic: From Shaoxi onward, the Three Duke posts were never again filled to full complement.

sentences.zh: 其後，韓仛胄、史彌遠、賈似道專政，皆至太師焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter Han Tuozhou, Shi Miyuan, and Jia Sidao dominated government, each rising to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Han Tuozhou, Shi Miyuan, and Jia Sidao seized power in turn, each ascended to the rank of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 宰相之職佐天子，總百官，平庶政，事無不統。

translations.literal: The chancellor's duty was to assist the Son of Heaven, oversee all officials, harmonize common administration, and unify all affairs without exception.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor assisted the emperor, commanded the bureaucracy, settled ordinary governance, and left no area of administration outside his purview.

sentences.zh: 宋承唐制，以同平章事為真相之任，無常員；

translations.literal: Song inherited Tang institutions, making Concurrent Grand Councilor the post of true chancellor, with no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Following Tang practice, the Song treated Concurrent Grand Councilor as the real chancellorship—a post with no standing numerical limit.

sentences.zh: 有二人，則分日知印。

translations.literal: When there were two, they divided days in managing the seal.
translations.idiomatic: When two chancellors served together, they took turns holding the seal on alternate days.

sentences.zh: 以丞、郎以上至三師為之。

translations.literal: Those from Vice Commissioner upward through the Three Masters could hold the post.
translations.idiomatic: The office could be filled by officials from Vice Commissioner rank up through the Three Masters.

sentences.zh: 其上相為昭文館大學士、監修國史，其次為集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: The senior chancellor was Hanlin Academician of the Hall for Adorning Literature and supervised the compilation of the national history; the next was Hanlin Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: The leading chancellor served as Hanlin Academician of the Hall for Adorning Literature and oversaw the national history; his junior counterpart held the Hanlin post at the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 或置三相，則昭文、集賢二學士並監修國史，各除。

translations.literal: If three chancellors were appointed, the Zhaowen and Jixian Hanlin academicians both supervised the national history, each separately appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When three chancellors were in place, the Hanlin posts at Zhaowen and Jixian halls jointly oversaw historiography, with each title conferred separately.

sentences.zh: 唐以來，三大館皆宰臣兼，故仍其制。

translations.literal: Since Tang times all three halls had been held concurrently by chancellors, so the old system was retained.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tang chancellors had long held all three hall posts concurrently, Song preserved that arrangement.

sentences.zh: 國初，範質昭文學士，王溥監修國史，魏仁浦集賢學士，此為三相例也。

translations.literal: At the founding, Fan Zhi was Zhaowen Academician, Wang Pu supervised the national history, and Wei Renpu was Jixian Academician—this established the precedent for three chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's earliest days Fan Zhi held Zhaowen Academician, Wang Pu supervised the national history, and Wei Renpu held Jixian Academician—thus setting the three-chancellor precedent.

sentences.zh: 神宗新官制，於三省置侍中、中書令、尚書令，以官高不除人，而以尚書令之貳左、右僕射為宰相。

translations.literal: Under Shenzong's new bureaucracy, Palace Attendant, Director of the Chancellery, and Director of the Department of State Affairs were placed in the Three Departments; because the ranks were too high to fill, the Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs served as chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong's bureaucratic reform installed Palace Attendant, Director of the Chancellery, and Director of the Department of State Affairs within the Three Departments. Those grand titles were left vacant, and the Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department actually performed the chancellor's work.

sentences.zh: 左僕射兼門下侍郎，以行侍中之職；

translations.literal: The Left Vice Director concurrently held Vice Minister of the Chancellery, performing the duties of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Vice Director doubled as Vice Minister of the Chancellery and discharged the functions of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 右僕射兼中書侍郎，以行中書令之職。

translations.literal: The Right Vice Director concurrently held Vice Minister of the Secretariat, performing the duties of Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Vice Director doubled as Vice Minister of the Secretariat and discharged the functions of Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 政和中，改左、右僕射為太宰、少宰，仍兼兩省侍郎。

translations.literal: During the Zhenghe era, the Left and Right Vice Directors were renamed Grand Minister and Vice Minister, still concurrently holding the two vice minister posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenghe period the Left and Right Vice Directors were retitled Grand Minister and Vice Minister while continuing to hold both vice ministerships.

sentences.zh: 靖康中，復改為左、右僕射。

translations.literal: During the Jingkang era, they were again changed back to Left and Right Vice Directors.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingkang the titles reverted to Left and Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，呂頤浩請參酌三省之制，左、右僕射並加同中書門下平章事，門下、中書二侍郎並改為參知政事，廢尚書左、右丞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, Lü Yihao requested harmonizing the Three Departments system: both Left and Right Vice Directors were additionally given Concurrent Director of the Chancellery and Secretariat Grand Councilor; both Vice Ministers of the Chancellery and Secretariat were changed to Vice Grand Councilors; and the Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 3 (1129), Lü Yihao proposed realigning the Three Departments: both Vice Directors would add Concurrent Director of the Chancellery and Secretariat Grand Councilor; the Chancellery and Secretariat Vice Ministers would become Vice Grand Councilors; and the Department's Left and Right Vice Directors would be eliminated.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 乾道八年，詔尚書左、右僕射可依漢制改為左、右丞相。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qiandao, an edict stated that the Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs might, following Han institutions, be changed to Left and Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 8 (1172), an edict authorized renaming the Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs as Left and Right Chancellor, following Han practice.

sentences.zh: 詳定敕令所言：“近承詔旨，改左、右僕射為左、右丞相，令刪去侍中、中書、尚書令，以左、右丞相充。

translations.literal: The commission for revising statutes and ordinances stated: "Recently, pursuant to an imperial order, the Left and Right Vice Directors were changed to Left and Right Chancellor, with Palace Attendant, Director of the Chancellery, and Director of the Department of State Affairs deleted and replaced by the Left and Right Chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: The commission revising statutes reported: "By recent edict the Left and Right Vice Directors became Left and Right Chancellor; the titles Palace Attendant, Director of the Chancellery, and Director of the Department of State Affairs were removed, and the two chancellors now filled those roles.

sentences.zh: 緣舊左、右僕射非三省長官，故為從一品。

translations.literal: Because the former Left and Right Vice Directors were not heads of the Three Departments, they ranked as second grade.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Left and Right Vice Directors had not been chiefs of the Three Departments and therefore held second-grade rank.

sentences.zh: 今左、右丞相系充侍中、中書、尚書令之位，即合為正一品。”

translations.literal: Now the Left and Right Chancellors occupy the posts of Palace Attendant, Director of the Chancellery, and Director of the Department of State Affairs, and therefore should rank as first grade.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Left and Right Chancellors now stood in for Palace Attendant, Director of the Chancellery, and Director of the Department of State Affairs, they properly belonged to first grade.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: This too was approved.

sentences.zh: 丞相官以太中大夫以上充。

translations.literal: The chancellor's office was filled by those of Grandee of Palace Personnel rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors were drawn from officials holding Grandee of Palace Personnel or higher rank.

sentences.zh: 使相親王、樞密使、留守、節度使兼侍中、中書令、同平章事者，皆謂之使相。

translations.literal: Imperial princes serving as commissioner-chancellors, Bureau of Military Affairs commissioners, military governors, and military commissioners concurrently holding Palace Attendant, Director of the Chancellery, or Concurrent Grand Councilor were all called military chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes, Bureau of Military Affairs commissioners, prefects-general, and military commissioners who concurrently held Palace Attendant, Director of the Chancellery, or Concurrent Grand Councilor were collectively termed military chancellors.

sentences.zh: 不預政事，不書敕，惟宣敕除授者，敕尾存其銜而已。

translations.literal: They did not participate in government affairs, did not sign edicts; only when edicts appointed them did their titles appear in the edict colophon.
translations.idiomatic: They took no part in policymaking and did not countersign edicts; when appointments were promulgated, their titles appeared only in the edict's closing lines.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，範質等三相皆罷，以趙普同平章事，李崇矩樞密使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande, all three chancellors including Fan Zhi were dismissed; Zhao Pu was made Concurrent Grand Councilor, and Li Chongju was made Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 2 (964), Fan Zhi and the other two chancellors were all removed; Zhao Pu became Concurrent Grand Councilor and Li Chongju Military Affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 命下，無宰相書敕，使問翰林陶谷。

translations.literal: When the order was issued, no chancellor was available to sign edicts; the emperor sent to ask Hanlin Academician Tao Gu.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment went out, no chancellor remained to countersign edicts, and the emperor consulted Hanlin Academician Tao Gu.

sentences.zh: 谷謂：“自昔輔相未嘗虛位。

translations.literal: Gu said: "Since antiquity the seats of chief ministers have never been left vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Gu replied: "From ancient times the chief minister's chair has never stood empty.

sentences.zh: 惟唐大和中甘露事，數日無宰相，時左僕射令狐楚等奉行制書。

translations.literal: Only during the Sweet Dew Incident in Tang Dahe were there several days without a chancellor, when Left Vice Director Linghu Chu and others carried out the edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The sole exception was the Sweet Dew Affair in Tang Dahe, when for several days no chancellor served and Left Vice Director Linghu Chu and others executed the edicts.

sentences.zh: 今尚書亦南省長官，可以書敕。”

translations.literal: Now the Director of the Department of State Affairs is also head of the southern department and may sign edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Director of the Department of State Affairs is likewise chief of the southern secretariat and may countersign edicts.

sentences.zh: 竇儀曰：“谷之所陳，非承平令典。

translations.literal: Dou Yi said: "What Gu has stated is not the standard of peaceful times.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi objected: "Gu's proposal is no precedent for a settled age.

sentences.zh: 今皇弟開封尹、同平章事，即宰相之任也，可書敕。”

translations.literal: The emperor's younger brother, Prefect of Kaifeng and Concurrent Grand Councilor—that is the chancellor's duty; he may sign edicts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's brother, Prefect of Kaifeng and Concurrent Grand Councilor, already holds the chancellor's office and may countersign edicts.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this view.

sentences.zh: 元豐新官制，廢參知政事，置門下、中書二侍郎，尚書左、右丞以代其任。

translations.literal: Under the Yuanfeng new bureaucracy, Vice Grand Councilors were abolished and Vice Ministers of the Chancellery and Secretariat were established; the Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs replaced their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfeng's reform eliminated Vice Grand Councilors, created Chancellery and Secretariat Vice Ministers, and assigned their former duties to the Department's Left and Right Vice Directors.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，復以門下、中書侍郎為參知政事，而省左、右丞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, the Chancellery and Secretariat Vice Ministers were again made Vice Grand Councilors, and the Department's Left and Right Vice Directors were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyan 3 restored the Chancellery and Secretariat Vice Ministers as Vice Grand Councilors and abolished the Department's Left and Right Vice Directors.

sentences.zh: 乾道八年，改左、右僕射為左、右丞相，其參知政事如故，以中大夫以上充，常除二員或一員。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qiandao, the Left and Right Vice Directors were changed to Left and Right Chancellor; Vice Grand Councilors remained as before, filled by those of Middle Court Grandee rank and above, usually one or two appointees.
translations.idiomatic: Qiandao 8 renamed the Left and Right Vice Directors as Left and Right Chancellor while Vice Grand Councilors continued unchanged, drawn from Middle Court Grandee upward, typically one or two at a time.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰三年，始除三員。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiatai, three appointees were first made.
translations.idiomatic: Jiatai 3 (1203) saw the first appointment of three Vice Grand Councilors at once.

sentences.zh: 故事，丞相謁告，參預不得進擬。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a chancellor took leave, participating vice councilors could not advance nominations.
translations.idiomatic: Custom held that while a chancellor was on leave, his participating deputies could not submit personnel recommendations.

sentences.zh: 惟丞相未除，則輪日當筆，然多不逾年，少僅旬月。

translations.literal: Only when no chancellor had yet been appointed did participating vice councilors rotate daily in wielding the brush; yet this seldom exceeded one year, and sometimes lasted only ten days or months.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the chancellorship stood vacant did vice councilors take turns drafting documents day by day—a situation that rarely lasted a full year and sometimes only ten days or a few months.

sentences.zh: 淳熙初，葉衡罷相，龔茂良行相事近三年，亦創見也。

translations.literal: Early in Chunxi, after Ye Heng was dismissed as chancellor, Gong Maoliang handled chancellor affairs for nearly three years—also an unprecedented case.
translations.idiomatic: Early Chunxi saw another rarity: after Ye Heng left office, Gong Maoliang acted as chancellor for nearly three years.

sentences.zh: 門下省受天下之成事，審命令，駁正違失，受發通進奏狀，進請寶印。

translations.literal: The Chancellery received completed business from throughout the realm, examined commands, corrected errors, received and forwarded memorial submissions, and advanced requests for the imperial seal.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery took in finished business from across the empire, scrutinized orders, rectified mistakes, handled incoming memorials, and forwarded petitions requiring the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 凡中書省畫黃、錄黃，樞密院錄白、畫旨，則留為底。

translations.literal: Whenever the Secretariat drafted yellow copies and recorded yellow, and the Bureau of Military Affairs recorded white and drafted intents, copies were retained as records.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow drafts and recorded yellow from the Secretariat, together with white records and drafted intents from the Bureau of Military Affairs, were all kept on file as master copies.

sentences.zh: 及尚書省六部所上有法式事，皆奏覆審駁之。

translations.literal: Legal matters submitted by the Six Ministries of the Department of State Affairs were all reported back for review and reexamination.
translations.idiomatic: Statutory cases forwarded by the Department's Six Ministries were all sent up for review and returned with scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 給事中讀，侍郎省，侍中審，進入被旨畫聞，則授之尚書省、樞密院。

translations.literal: After the Supervising Censor read them, the Vice Minister reviewed, the Palace Attendant examined, and upon receiving imperial approval they were noted and announced, then transmitted to the Department of State Affairs and Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Supervising Censor read each document, the Vice Minister checked it, the Palace Attendant approved it, and once imperial assent was recorded and proclaimed, it passed to the Department of State Affairs and the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 即有舛誤應舉駁者，大則論列，不則改正。

translations.literal: If there were errors warranting challenge, major ones were argued in memorial; minor ones were corrected.
translations.idiomatic: When mistakes required objection, grave cases were debated in memorial; lesser ones were simply amended.

sentences.zh: 凡文書自內降者，著之籍。

translations.literal: Documents descending from within the palace were entered in the register.
translations.idiomatic: All paperwork issued from the inner court was logged in the registry.

sentences.zh: 章奏至，則受而通進，俟頒降，分送所隸官司。

translations.literal: When memorials arrived, they were received and forwarded; after promulgation they were distributed to the agencies under their jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Incoming memorials were received and relayed upward; once the court's response was issued, copies went to the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 凡吏部擬六品以下職事官，則給事中校其仕歷、功狀，侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Personnel proposed officials below sixth rank, the Supervising Censor checked their service records and merit dossiers, and the Vice Minister reviewed.
translations.idiomatic: For Ministry of Personnel nominations to posts below sixth rank, the Supervising Censor verified service histories and merit records, and the Vice Minister examined the file.

sentences.zh: 侍中引驗審察，非其人則論奏。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant led verification and inspection; if the person was unsuitable, a memorial was submitted arguing the case.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant personally reviewed the candidate; if unfit, he memorialized against the appointment.

sentences.zh: 凡遷改爵秩、加敘勛封、四選擬註奏鈔之事，有舛誤，退送尚書省。

translations.literal: For transfers and rank changes, additions of honors and enfeoffments, the four selection tracks' nomination slips—if there were errors they were returned to the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Errors in promotions, ennoblements, merit grants, or nomination documents from the four selection circuits were sent back to the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 覆刑部大理寺所斷獄，審其輕重枉直，不當罪，則以法駁正之。

translations.literal: It reviewed verdicts handed down by the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review, examining whether punishments were too light, too heavy, or unjust; when the crime did not fit, they were corrected according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery reexamined sentences from the Ministry of Justice and Court of Judicial Review, weighing proportion and fairness; improper verdicts were overturned by statute.

sentences.zh: 國初循舊制，以中書門下平章事為宰相之職，復用兩制官一員判門下省事。

translations.literal: At the founding the old system was followed, with Concurrent Director of the Chancellery and Secretariat Grand Councilor as the chancellor's office, and one drafter official assigned to oversee Chancellery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early on the dynasty kept the old arrangement: Concurrent Director of the Chancellery and Secretariat Grand Councilor served as chancellor, while a single drafter from the two academies supervised Chancellery business.

sentences.zh: 官制行，始釐正焉。

translations.literal: When the new bureaucracy took effect, this was rectified.
translations.idiomatic: The new official system finally regularized that practice.

sentences.zh: 凡官十有一：侍中、侍郎、左散騎常侍各一人，給事中四人，左諫議大夫、起居郎、左司諫、左正言各一人。

translations.literal: In all there were eleven offices: one each of Palace Attendant, Vice Minister, and Left Regular Attendant; four Supervising Censors; and one each of Left Remonstrating Censor, Left Diary Officer, Left Secretariat Remonstrator, and Left Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven posts made up the staff: Palace Attendant, Vice Minister, and Left Regular Attendant, one each; four Supervising Censors; and one Left Remonstrating Censor, Left Diary Officer, Left Secretariat Remonstrator, and Left Censor.

sentences.zh: 先是，中書人吏分掌五房：曰孔目房、吏房、戶房、兵禮房、刑房；

translations.literal: Previously, Secretariat clerks were divided to manage five sections, called the General Matters Section, Personnel Section, Household Section, Military and Rites Section, and Penal Section.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Secretariat clerks had been split among five desks—General Matters, Personnel, Household, Military and Rites, and Penal.

sentences.zh: 又有主事、勾銷二房。

translations.literal: There were also Chief Clerk and Verification sections.
translations.idiomatic: Two additional sections handled chief clerical work and final verification.

sentences.zh: 至是，釐中書為三省，分兵與禮為六房，各因其省之事而增益之。

translations.literal: At this point the Chancellery was reorganized into the Three Departments; military and rites were split into six sections, each augmented according to its department's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery was then sorted into the Three Departments framework; military and rites were separated into six sections, each expanded to match its parent department's workload.

sentences.zh: 門下凡分房十：曰吏房，曰戶房，曰禮房，曰兵房，曰刑房，曰工房，皆視其房之名，而主行尚書省六曹二十四司所上之事；

translations.literal: Under the Chancellery there were ten sections in all: Personnel, Household, Rites, Military, Penal, and Works—each, according to its name, handled matters submitted by the corresponding bureaus of the Six Ministries' twenty-four departments.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery itself ran ten sections—Personnel, Household, Rites, Military, Penal, and Works—each processing submissions from the matching bureaus within the Six Ministries' twenty-four departments.

sentences.zh: 曰開拆房，曰章奏房，曰制敕庫房，亦皆視其名，而受遣文書、表狀，與供閱敕令格式、擬官爵封勛之類，惟班簿、本省雜務則歸吏房。

translations.literal: There were also the Opening Section, Memorial Section, and Edict Archive Section—each likewise named for its function—receiving and dispatching documents and memorials, supplying edicts, statutes, and formats for review, and drafting ennoblements, titles, and merit grants; only roster books and miscellaneous internal business belonged to the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: Opening, Memorial, and Edict Archive sections handled incoming and outgoing paperwork, memorials, and reference copies of edicts and regulations, plus drafts for titles, enfeoffments, and honors; roster ledgers and internal housekeeping alone fell to the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 吏四十有九：錄事、主事各三人，令史六人，書令史十有八人，守當官十有九人。

translations.literal: Clerks numbered forty-nine within: three Recorders and three Chief Clerks each, six Clerks, eighteen Writing Clerks, and nineteen Duty Officers.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-nine staff served inside the office—three Recorders, three Chief Clerks, six Clerks, eighteen Writing Clerks, and nineteen Duty Officers.

sentences.zh: 而外省吏十有九人：令史一人，書令史二人，守當官六人，守闕守當官十人。

translations.literal: Outside the department there were nineteen clerks: one Clerk, two Writing Clerks, six Duty Officers, and ten Reserve Duty Officers.
translations.idiomatic: The outer Chancellery staff numbered nineteen: one Clerk, two Writing Clerks, six Duty Officers, and ten Reserve Duty Officers.

sentences.zh: 元豐八年，以門下、中書外省為後省，門下外省復置催驅房。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanfeng, the outer sections of the Chancellery and Secretariat were made the Rear Department; the Chancellery's outer section again established an Expediting Section.
translations.idiomatic: the eighth year of Yuanfeng redesignated the outer offices of Chancellery and Secretariat as the Rear Department and restored an Expediting Section in the Chancellery's outer office.

sentences.zh: 元祐三年，詔吏部註通判，赴門下引驗；

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanyou, an edict ordered that transit magistrates registered by the Ministry of Personnel undergo verification at the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou 3 required transit magistrates nominated by the Ministry of Personnel to appear at the Chancellery for credential review.

sentences.zh: 應省、台、寺、監諸司人吏四分減一。

translations.literal: Clerks in the departments, censorate, courts, and commissions were reduced by one quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Staff in the secretariats, censorate, courts, and supervisory commissions were cut by twenty-five percent.

sentences.zh: 復置點檢房。

translations.literal: The Inspection Section was restored.
translations.idiomatic: An Inspection Section was reinstated.

sentences.zh: 四年，又別立吏額。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, separate clerk quotas were again established.
translations.idiomatic: The following year new staffing quotas were set independently.

sentences.zh: 紹聖二年，守闕守當官，門下、中書省各以百人，尚書省百五十人為額。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaosheng, Reserve Duty Officers were capped at one hundred each for the Chancellery and Secretariat, and one hundred fifty for the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shaosheng 2 fixed Reserve Duty Officer quotas at one hundred for each of the Chancellery and Secretariat and one hundred fifty for the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，三省吏員並依元豐七年額。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, clerk quotas for all Three Departments were restored to the Yuanfeng seventh-year levels.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later, staffing levels across all Three Departments reverted to the quotas of the seventh year of Yuanfeng.

sentences.zh: 侍中掌佐天子議大政，審中外出納之事。
