translations.literal: The Palace Attendant assisted the Son of Heaven in deliberating great affairs and examining matters of receiving and dispatching within and without the department.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant assisted the emperor in deliberating major policy and supervised all incoming and outgoing business of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 大祭祀則版奏中嚴外辦，導輿輅，詔升降之節；

translations.literal: At great sacrifices he would announce with the clapper inner solemnity and outer preparation, lead the imperial carriage, and proclaim the protocols of ascent and descent.
translations.idiomatic: At major sacrifices he signaled the inner and outer ceremonial stages, led the imperial carriage, and directed the prescribed movements of ascent and descent.

sentences.zh: 皇帝齋則請就齋室。

translations.literal: When the emperor observed abstention, he would request him to enter the abstention chamber.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor undertook ritual fasting, he invited him to retire to the fasting chamber.

sentences.zh: 大朝會則承旨宣制、告成禮，祭祀亦如之。

translations.literal: At great court assemblies he received the imperial intent and proclaimed edicts, announcing completion of the rites; at sacrifices it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: At grand court audiences he received the emperor's instruction to proclaim edicts and announce the completion of ceremony—the same at sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 冊後則奉寶以授司徒。

translations.literal: Upon investiture of an empress he presented the seal to confer upon the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: At an empress's investiture he presented the imperial seal and entrusted it to the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 國朝以秩高罕除。

translations.literal: In our dynasty, because the rank was high, appointments were rarely made.
translations.idiomatic: Because the rank was so exalted, the dynasty seldom filled the post.

sentences.zh: 知建隆至熙寧，真拜侍中才五人，雖有用他官兼領，而實不任其事。

translations.literal: From Jianlong through Xining, those truly appointed Palace Attendant numbered only five; although other offices were used to hold concurrent appointment, in reality they did not discharge the duties.
translations.idiomatic: From Jianlong through Xining, only five men received genuine appointment as Palace Attendant; others held the title concurrently without actually performing the office.

sentences.zh: 官制行，以左僕射兼門下侍郎行侍中職，別置侍郎以佐之。

translations.literal: When the new offices took effect, the Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs concurrently serving as Chancellery Vice Minister discharged Palace Attendant duties, and a separate Vice Minister was established to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Under the reformed offices, the Left Vice Director of the Department concurrently serving as Chancellery Vice Minister performed the duties of Palace Attendant, with a separately appointed Vice Minister to assist.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，置左、右丞相，省侍中不置。

translations.literal: After the southward crossing, Left and Right Chancellors were established, and the Palace Attendant office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After the court's relocation south, Left and Right Chancellors were installed and the Palace Attendant post was eliminated.

sentences.zh: 侍郎 掌貳侍中之職，省中外出納之事。

translations.literal: The Vice Minister managed the secondary duties of the Palace Attendant and the department's incoming and outgoing business.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Minister served as the Palace Attendant's deputy and oversaw the Chancellery's documentary traffic.

sentences.zh: 大祭祀則前導輿略，詔進止。

translations.literal: At great sacrifices he led the imperial carriage in advance, proclaiming advance and halt.
translations.idiomatic: At major sacrifices he went ahead to guide the imperial carriage and directed when to proceed or stop.

sentences.zh: 大朝賀則授表以奏祥瑞。

translations.literal: At great court felicitations he presented the memorial to report auspicious omens.
translations.idiomatic: At grand congratulatory audiences he received and submitted the memorial reporting auspicious portents.

sentences.zh: 冊後則奉節及寶位。

translations.literal: Upon empress investiture he presented the staff of authority and the seal of office.
translations.idiomatic: At an empress's investiture he bore the ceremonial staff and imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 與知樞密院、同知樞密院、中書侍郎、尚書左右丞為執政官。

translations.literal: Together with the Commissioner and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, the Secretariat Vice Minister, and the Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs, he ranked as a chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He stood among the serving chief administrators alongside the Commissioner and Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, the Secretariat Vice Minister, and the Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，復置參知政事，省門下侍郎不置。

translations.literal: After the southward crossing, Vice Grand Councilors were restored, and the Chancellery Vice Minister was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After the relocation south, Vice Grand Councilors were reinstated and the Chancellery Vice Minister post was dropped.

sentences.zh: 左散騎常侍 左諫議大夫 左司諫 左正言 同掌規諫諷諭。

translations.literal: The Left Regular Attendant, Left Remonstrance Grandee, Left Supervising Remonstrance Official, and Left Corrective Official together managed regulation, remonstrance, and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Regular Attendant, Left Remonstrance Grandee, Left Supervising Remonstrance Official, and Left Corrective Official jointly handled oversight, remonstrance, and admonitory counsel.

sentences.zh: 凡朝政闕失、大臣至百官任非其人、三省至百司事有違失，皆得諫正。

translations.literal: Whenever court policy had defects, ministers down to ordinary officials held posts unsuited to them, or the Three Departments down to all agencies had violations or errors, remonstrance and correction were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: They could remonstrate against flaws in court policy, unsuitable appointments from ministers down to common officials, and violations anywhere from the Three Departments to every agency.

sentences.zh: 國初雖置諫院，知院官凡六人，以司諫、正言充職；

translations.literal: At the dynasty's founding a Remonstrance Bureau was established; the directors numbered six, filled by Supervising Remonstrance Officials and Corrective Officials.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty a Remonstrance Bureau was set up with six directors drawn from the ranks of Supervising Remonstrance Officials and Corrective Officials.

sentences.zh: 而他官領者，謂之知諫院。

translations.literal: When other officials held it, they were called Directors of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Officials from other posts who headed it were styled Directors of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 正言、司諫亦有領他職而不預諫諍者。

translations.literal: Corrective Officials and Supervising Remonstrance Officials also sometimes held other posts and did not participate in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Some Corrective Officials and Supervising Remonstrance Officials held concurrent duties and took no part in remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 官制行，始皆正名。

translations.literal: When the new offices took effect, they all at last received their proper titles.
translations.idiomatic: With the office reform, each post finally received its formal designation.

sentences.zh: 元豐八年，諫議大夫孫覺言：“據《官制格目》，諫官之職，凡發令舉事，有不便於時，不合於道，大則廷議，小則上封。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanfeng, Remonstrance Grandee Sun Jue said: "According to the Office Regulations Manual, the duty of remonstrance officials is that whenever orders are issued or undertakings begun that are untimely or contrary to the Way, for major matters debate in court, for minor matters submit a sealed memorial.
translations.idiomatic: the eighth year of Yuanfeng: Remonstrance Grandee Sun Jue argued, "Under the "Office Regulations Manual," remonstrance officials should debate major orders or actions that are ill-timed or improper in open court, and submit sealed memorials on lesser ones.

sentences.zh: 若賢良之遺滯於下，忠孝之不聞於上，則以事狀論薦，乞依此以修舉職事。”

translations.literal: If the worthy and good languished below while loyalty and filial piety went unheard above, then by written report recommend them; I request that duties be carried out accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: When worthy talent languished below or loyal and filial service went unrewarded above, they should recommend such cases in detailed reports—I ask that our duties be restored on this basis.

sentences.zh: 八月，門下省言：“諫議大夫、司諫、正言合通為一。”

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Chancellery stated: "The Remonstrance Grandee, Supervising Remonstrance Official, and Corrective Official should be combined into one office."
translations.idiomatic: August: the Chancellery reported, "The Remonstrance Grandee, Supervising Remonstrance Official, and Corrective Official ought to be treated as one consolidated function."

sentences.zh: 詔並從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved both proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved both recommendations.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔仿《六典》置諫官員。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, an edict ordered establishing remonstrance officials modeled on the Six Canon.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month: an edict restored remonstrance posts along the lines of the Tang Six Codes.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年二月，詔諫官雖不同省，許二人同上殿。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Yuanyou, an edict allowed two remonstrance officials from different departments to ascend the hall together.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou 1, second month: remonstrance officials from different departments were permitted to appear before the throne two at a time.

sentences.zh: 後又從司諫虞策之請，如獨員，許與台官同對。

translations.literal: Later, at the request of Supervising Remonstrance Official Yu Ce, when only a single incumbent, he was allowed to address the throne jointly with a censorate official.
translations.idiomatic: Later, upon Supervising Remonstrance Official Yu Ce's petition, a sole remonstrance officer was allowed to appear jointly with censorate officials.

sentences.zh: 九月，左、右正言久闕，侍御史王岩叟言：“國家仿近古之制，諫官六員，方之先王，已自為少，望詔補足，無令久空職。”

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Left and Right Corrective Officials had long been vacant; Supervising Censor Wang Yansou said: "The state follows the recent ancient system with six remonstrance posts—compared to former kings this is already few; I hope an edict will fill the vacancies and not leave posts empty long."
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: with both Corrective Official posts long unfilled, Supervising Censor Wang Yansou urged, "The dynasty follows antiquity with only six remonstrance officers—already fewer than the sage kings allotted; please order the vacancies filled promptly."

sentences.zh: 十月，司諫王覿言：“自今中書舍人闕，勿以諫官兼權。”

translations.literal: In the tenth month Supervising Remonstrance Official Wang Di said: "From now on when the Secretariat Drafting Official is vacant, do not assign remonstrance officials concurrently in an acting capacity."
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month: Supervising Remonstrance Official Wang Di proposed, "Whenever a Secretariat Drafting Officialship falls vacant, remonstrance officials must no longer fill it on an acting basis."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，岩叟又言：“近降聖旨，兩省諫官各令出入異戶，勿與給事中、中書舍人通。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yansou again said: "A recent imperial decree ordered remonstrance officials of both departments to enter and exit by separate gates and not associate with Supervising Censors and Secretariat Drafting Officials.
translations.idiomatic: November: Wang Yansou added, "A recent decree ordered remonstrance officials in both departments to use separate entrances and avoid contact with Supervising Censors and Secretariat Drafting Officials.

sentences.zh: 實欲限隔諫官，不使在政事之地，恐知本末，數論列爾。”

translations.literal: The real aim was to isolate remonstrance officials, keep them from the seat of governance, fearing they would learn the full story and repeatedly argue the point.
translations.idiomatic: The intent was to isolate remonstrance officers from the inner policy circle so they would not learn the full facts and raise repeated objections.

sentences.zh: 尋詔諫官直舍仍舊。

translations.literal: Soon an edict restored the remonstrance officials' duty rooms to the former arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an edict restored the remonstrance officers' quarters to their former arrangement.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔執政親戚不除諫官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict ordered that relatives of chief administrators not be appointed remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, an edict barred appointment of remonstrance officials from among chief administrators' kin.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國元年，言者謂諫官論事，惟憑詢訪，而百司之事，六曹所報外，皆不得其詳。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo, speakers said remonstrance officials deliberated affairs relying only on inquiry, while matters of the hundred offices beyond what the Six Sections reported could not be learned in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhong Jingguo 1: critics noted that remonstrance officials had to rely on inquiry alone and could not obtain full details on agency business beyond the Six Sections' reports.

sentences.zh: 遂詔諫官案許關台察。

translations.literal: An edict then allowed the Remonstrance Section to consult the censorate's investigative files.
translations.idiomatic: The court then authorized the Remonstrance Section to access censorate investigation files.

sentences.zh: 給事中 四人，分治六房，掌讀中外出納，及判後省之事。

translations.literal: Four Supervising Censors, divided among the six sections, managed reading of incoming and outgoing documents within and without, and adjudicated Rear Department business.
translations.idiomatic: Four Supervising Censors, each assigned to one of six sections, reviewed Chancellery documents and adjudicated Rear Department business.

sentences.zh: 若政令有失當，除授非其人，則論奏而駁正之。

translations.literal: If policies were improper or appointments unsuitable, they memorialized arguing and returned them for correction.
translations.idiomatic: When edicts were improper or appointments unsuitable, they memorialized objections and demanded correction.

sentences.zh: 凡章奏，日錄目以進，考其稽違而糾治之。

translations.literal: All memorials were logged daily by item and submitted; delays were examined and offenders punished.
translations.idiomatic: They logged every memorial daily, tracked delays, and disciplined those responsible.

sentences.zh: 故事，詔旨皆付銀台司封駁。

translations.literal: By precedent, all edicts were sent to the Silver Terrace Office for seal-and-return review.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly all edicts went to the Silver Terrace Office for seal-and-return review.

sentences.zh: 官制行，給事中始正其職，而封駁司歸門下。

translations.literal: When the new offices took effect, Supervising Censors at last received their proper duties, and the seal-and-return office returned to the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Under the office reform, Supervising Censors finally exercised their proper functions and seal-and-return review reverted to the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年五月，詔給事中許書畫黃，不書草，著為令。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year of Yuanfeng, an edict allowed Supervising Censors to sign yellow drafts but not draft them, established as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: the fifth year of Yuanfeng, fifth month: Supervising Censors were authorized to sign finalized yellow copies but not draft them—a rule formally codified.

sentences.zh: 六月，給事中陸佃言：“三省、密院文字，已讀者尚令封駁，慮失之重覆。”。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Supervising Censor Lu Dian said: "Documents of the Three Departments and Military Affairs Bureau, already read, are still subject to seal-and-return review—I fear this creates redundant duplication.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: Supervising Censor Lu Dian warned that requiring seal-and-return on documents the Three Departments and Military Bureau had already read risked needless duplication.

sentences.zh: 詔罷封駁房。

translations.literal: An edict abolished the Seal-and-Return Section.
translations.idiomatic: The court abolished the Seal-and-Return Section.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔駁正事赴執政稟議。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered that matters of correction and return go to chief administrators for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth year: returned corrections had to be submitted to chief administrators for prior consultation.

sentences.zh: 七年，有旨，舉駁事，依中書舍人封還詞頭例。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an order stated that matters of objection should follow the precedent of Secretariat Drafting Officials returning draft appointment documents.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh year: the throne ruled that objections should follow the precedent of Secretariat Drafting Officials returning appointment drafts.

sentences.zh: 既而令稟議如初，給事中韓忠彥言：“給、舍職位頗均，一則不稟白而聽封還，一則許舉駁而先稟議，於理未允。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the prior consultation rule was restored; Supervising Censor Han Zhongyan said: "Supervising Censor and Drafting Official ranks are much alike—one may return drafts without consulting, while the other must consult before objecting; this is unreasonable.
translations.idiomatic: The consultation requirement was soon restored, prompting Supervising Censor Han Zhongyan to argue: "Supervising Censor and Drafting Official are peers—yet one may return drafts without reporting while the other must consult before objecting; that is inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 且朝廷之事執政所行，職當封駁則已與執政異，自當求決於上，尚何稟議之有？”

translations.literal: Moreover court business is conducted by chief administrators; the duty of seal-and-return already puts one at odds with them—one should seek decision from above; why still consult?
translations.idiomatic: State business belongs to the chief administrators; seal-and-return already puts us at odds with them—we should appeal directly to the throne. Why consult the administrators at all?

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年，葉祖洽言：“兩省置給、舍，使之互察。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaosheng, Ye Zuzhi said: "Both departments established Supervising Censor and Drafting Official for mutual oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Shaosheng 4: Ye Zuzhi observed, "The two departments created parallel Supervising Censor and Drafting Official posts precisely for mutual oversight.

sentences.zh: 今中書舍人兼權封駁，則給事中之職遂廢。”

translations.literal: Now with the Secretariat Drafting Official concurrently holding seal-and-return authority, the Supervising Censor's function is abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Secretariat Drafting Officials hold concurrent seal-and-return authority, the Supervising Censor's role is effectively abolished.

sentences.zh: 詔特旨書讀不迴避，餘互書判。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that special-edict readings need not be recused; the rest would mutually sign and review.
translations.idiomatic: An edict exempted special-edict readings from recusal but required mutual signing on all other documents.

sentences.zh: 元符三年，翰林學士曾肇言：“門下之職，所以駁正中書違失。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfu, Hanlin Academician Zeng Zhao said: "The Chancellery's duty is to correct Secretariat errors.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu 3: Hanlin Academician Zeng Zhao argued, "The Chancellery exists to correct Secretariat errors.

sentences.zh: 近日給事封駁中書錄黃，乃令舍人書讀行下，隳壞官制，有損治體。

translations.literal: Recently when the Supervising Censor sealed and returned the Secretariat's recorded yellow, the Drafting Official was made to sign and read for promulgation—destroying the office system and harming governance.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, after a Supervising Censor returned a Secretariat yellow copy, a Drafting Official was allowed to sign and promulgate it—undermining the office system and the structure of government.

sentences.zh: 願正紀綱，為天下後世法。”

translations.literal: I wish to restore discipline and regulation as a model for the realm and posterity.
translations.idiomatic: I urge restoration of proper procedure as a model for the realm and posterity.

sentences.zh: 重和元年，給事中張叔夜言：“凡命令之出，中書宣奉，門下審讀，然後付尚書頒行，而密院被旨者，亦錄付門下，此神宗官制也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chonghe, Supervising Censor Zhang Shuye said: "Whenever commands issue, the Secretariat announces and presents, the Chancellery examines and reads, then they are sent to the Department for promulgation; orders received by the Military Bureau are also recorded and sent to the Chancellery—this was Emperor Shenzong's office system.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghe 1: Supervising Censor Zhang Shuye noted, "Under Shenzong's system every command went from Secretariat announcement through Chancellery review before the Department promulgated it, and Military Bureau orders were also recorded to the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 今急速文字，不經三省，而諸房以空黃先次書讀， 則審讀殆成虛設矣，乞立法禁。”

translations.literal: Now urgent documents bypass the Three Departments, while sections sign and read blank yellow copies first—the examination and reading is nearly void; I request statutory prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Today urgent documents bypass the Three Departments while sections pre-sign blank yellow copies, rendering review a mere formality—I ask that this be banned by statute.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 凡分案五：曰上案，主寶禮及朝會所行事；

translations.literal: There were five sections in all: the Upper Section managed seals, ceremonies, and court assembly affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Work was divided into five sections: the Upper Section managed seals, ceremonies, and court audiences;

sentences.zh: 曰下案，主受發文書；

translations.literal: the Lower Section managed receiving and dispatching documents;
translations.idiomatic: the Lower Section handled incoming and outgoing documents;

sentences.zh: 曰封駁案，主封駁及試吏，校其功過；

translations.literal: the Seal-and-Return Section managed seal-and-return review and testing clerks, assessing merit and fault;
translations.idiomatic: the Seal-and-Return Section handled seal-and-return review and clerk examinations;

sentences.zh: 曰諫官案，主關報文書；

translations.literal: the Remonstrance Section managed liaison and reporting documents;
translations.idiomatic: the Remonstrance Section handled liaison reports;

sentences.zh: 曰記註案，主錄起居註。

translations.literal: the Diary Section managed recording the Diary of Activity and Repose.
translations.idiomatic: the Diary Section maintained the Diary of Activity and Repose.

sentences.zh: 其雜務則所分案掌焉。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous duties were managed by the assigned sections.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous duties fell to whichever section was assigned.

sentences.zh: 紹興以後，止除二人或一人。

translations.literal: After Shaoxing, only two or one were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shaoxing era, only one or two Supervising Censors were appointed.

sentences.zh: 起居郎 一人，掌記天子言動。

translations.literal: One Diarist recorded the emperor's words and deeds.
translations.idiomatic: One Diarist recorded the emperor's words and actions.

sentences.zh: 御殿則侍立，行幸則從，大朝會則與起居舍人對立於殿下螭首之側。

translations.literal: When the emperor held court he stood in attendance; on journeys he followed; at great assemblies he stood opposite the Diarist-at-Large beside the dragon-head platform.
translations.idiomatic: He stood attendance in the hall, accompanied imperial tours, and at grand audiences stood opposite the Diarist-at-Large beside the dragon-head platform steps.

sentences.zh: 凡朝廷命令赦宥、禮樂法度損益因革、賞罰勸懲、群臣進對、文武臣除授及祭祀宴享、臨幸引見之事，四時氣候、四方符瑞、戶口增減、州縣廢置，皆書以授著作官。

translations.literal: All court commands and amnesties, ritual and law changes, rewards and punishments, ministers' audiences, civil and military appointments, sacrifices, banquets, imperial visits and audiences, seasons and climate, portents from the four quarters, population changes, and abolition or establishment of prefectures and counties—all were written and handed to the Compilation Office.
translations.idiomatic: He recorded edicts, amnesties, ritual and legal reforms, rewards and punishments, ministerial audiences, appointments, sacrifices, banquets, imperial outings, seasons, portents, population shifts, and changes in prefectures and counties, passing all entries to the Compilation Office.

sentences.zh: 國朝舊置起居院，命三館校理以上修起居註。

translations.literal: The dynasty once established an Activity-and-Repose Bureau, appointing Hanlin collators and above to compile the diary.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty once maintained an Activity-and-Repose Bureau, assigning Hanlin collators and higher to compile the diary.

sentences.zh: 熙寧四年，詔諫官兼修註者，因後殿侍立，許奏事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xining, an edict stated that remonstrance officials who also compiled the diary, while attending in the rear hall, were permitted to address the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Xining 4: remonstrance officials who doubled as diary compilers were allowed to address the throne while attending in the rear hall.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年，兼修註王存乞復起居郎、舍人之職，使得盡聞明天子德音，退而書之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng, diary compiler Wang Cun requested restoring the Diarist and Diarist-at-Large posts so that they could fully hear the Son of Heaven's virtuous words and write them upon withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: the second year of Yuanfeng: diary compiler Wang Cun petitioned to restore dedicated Diarist and Diarist-at-Large posts so compilers could hear the emperor's words fully and write them down afterward.

sentences.zh: 神宗亦謂：“人臣奏對有頗僻讒慝者，若左右有史官書之，則無所肆其姦矣。”

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong also said: "When ministers answering at audience speak perversely or slanderously, if historians at their side record it, they would have no room to freely commit villainy."
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong likewise observed, "When ministers speak perversely or slanderously at audience, historians standing by would deter such conduct."

sentences.zh: 然未果行。

translations.literal: Yet it was not yet carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The reform was not enacted.

sentences.zh: 故事，左、右史雖日侍立，而欲奏事，必稟中書俟旨。

translations.literal: By precedent, though the Left and Right Historians attended daily, wishing to address the throne they had to report to the Secretariat and await instruction.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, though Left and Right Historians attended daily, they had to apply to the Secretariat and await permission before addressing the throne.

sentences.zh: 存因對及之。

translations.literal: Cun raised this while answering at audience.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cun raised the matter during an imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 八月，乃詔雖不兼諫職，許直前奏事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, an edict stated that even without concurrent remonstrance duty, advancing directly to address the throne was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: That August, an edict authorized direct audience even without concurrent remonstrance duties.

sentences.zh: 蓋存發之也。

translations.literal: This was initiated by Cun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cun had originated the change.

sentences.zh: 官制行，改修註為郎、舍人。

translations.literal: When the new offices took effect, diary compilation was changed to Diarist and Diarist-at-Large posts.
translations.idiomatic: Under the office reform, diary compilation was assigned to dedicated Diarist and Diarist-at-Large posts.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔左、右史分記言動；

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered the Left and Right Historians to record words and deeds separately;
translations.idiomatic: the sixth year of Yuanfeng ordered Left and Right Historians to record the emperor's words and actions separately;

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，仍詔不分。

translations.literal: in the first year of Yuanyou, an edict still ordered that they not be divided.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou 1 reversed this and restored joint recording.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔邇英閣講讀罷，有留身奏事者，許侍立。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict stated that after lecturing at the Zhiying Pavilion ended, if someone remained to address the throne, attendance was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou 7: after lectures at the Zhiying Pavilion, historians were permitted to remain standing when the emperor held private audience.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，中丞黃履言：“所奏或乾機密，難令旁立，仍依先朝故事。”

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng, Censor-in-Chief Huang Lu said: "What is addressed may touch secrets; it is hard to have others stand nearby—still follow the former dynasty's precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Shaosheng 1: Censor-in-Chief Huang Lu argued that private audience might touch state secrets and historians should not stand nearby—restore the former practice.

sentences.zh: 先是，御後殿則左、右史分日侍立；

translations.literal: Previously, when holding court in the rear hall the Left and Right Historians attended on alternating days;
translations.idiomatic: Previously, at the rear hall Left and Right Historians had attended on alternating days;

sentences.zh: 崇寧三年，詔如前殿之儀，更不分日。

translations.literal: in the third year of Chongning, an edict followed the front hall protocol and no longer divided the days.
translations.idiomatic: Chongning 3 restored the front-hall rule that both attended daily without alternation.

sentences.zh: 大觀元年，詔事有足以勸善懲惡者，雖秩卑亦書之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daguan, an edict stated that matters sufficient to encourage good and punish evil, even if rank was low, were also to be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Daguan 1 ordered that noteworthy deeds of moral encouragement or warning be recorded regardless of the subject's rank.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十八年，用起居郎洪遵言，起居郎、舍人自今後許依講讀官奏事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Shaoxing, following Diarist Hong Zun's proposal, Diarists and Diarists-at-Large from then on were permitted to address the throne like lecturing officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 28 adopted Diarist Hong Zun's proposal allowing Diarists and Diarists-at-Large to address the throne like lecture officials.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，用起居郎兼侍講胡銓言，前殿依後殿輪左、右史侍立。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing, following Court Diarist and Concurrent Lecturer Hu Quan's proposal, at the front hall the Left and Right Historians would attend on alternating days as at the rear hall.
translations.idiomatic: Longxing 1 adopted Court Diarist Hu Quan's proposal to alternate Left and Right Historians at the front hall as at the rear hall.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎 二人，掌外廷符寶之事。

translations.literal: Two Seal-and-Credential Attendants managed outer-court seals and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: Two attendants were charged with the outer court's seals and credentials.

sentences.zh: 禁中別有內符寶郎。

translations.literal: Within the forbidden precinct there were separate Inner Seal-and-Credential Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace maintained its own attendants for seals and credentials.

sentences.zh: 官制行，未嘗除。

translations.literal: When the new offices took effect, the post was never filled.
translations.idiomatic: Under the office reform the post was never filled.

sentences.zh: 大觀初，八寶成，詔依《唐六典》增置。

translations.literal: Early in the Daguan era, when the Eight Imperial Treasures were completed, an edict ordered additions per the Tang Six Codes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daguan era, when the Eight Imperial Treasures were completed, posts were added per the "Tang Six Codes."

sentences.zh: 靖康罷之。

translations.literal: In the Jingkang reign they were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The posts were abolished in the Jingkang reign.

sentences.zh: 通進司 隸給事中，掌受三省、樞密院、六曹、寺監百司奏牘，文武近臣表疏及章奏房所領天下章奏案牘，具事目進呈，而頒佈於中外。

translations.literal: The Document Relay Office, subordinate to the Supervising Censor, received memorials from the Three Departments, Bureau of Military Affairs, Six Ministries, courts, commissions, and all agencies, plus memorials from civil and military officials near the throne and the empire-wide memorial files managed by the Memorial Section; it compiled item lists for presentation and promulgated them within and beyond the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Document Relay Office, under the Supervising Censor, took in memorials from the Three Departments, Military Bureau, Six Ministries, courts, commissions, and all agencies, together with near-court officials' petitions and empire-wide memorial files from the Memorial Section, compiled itemized lists for presentation, and distributed copies inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 進奏院 隸給事中，掌受詔敕及三省、樞密院宣扎，六曹、寺監百司符牒，頒於諸路。

translations.literal: The Memorial Submission Office, subordinate to the Supervising Censor, received edicts and orders from the Three Departments and Bureau of Military Affairs and dispatches from the Six Ministries, courts, commissions, and all agencies, promulgating them to the circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The Memorial Submission Office, also under the Supervising Censor, received edicts and orders from the Three Departments and Military Bureau and dispatches from the Six Ministries, courts, and agencies, promulgating them to the circuits.

sentences.zh: 凡章奏至，則具事目上門下省。

translations.literal: When memorials arrived, item lists were compiled and submitted to the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Arriving memorials were logged by item and forwarded to the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 若案牘及申稟文書，則分納諸官司。

translations.literal: Case files and application documents were distributed to the various agencies.
translations.idiomatic: Case files and application documents were routed to the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 凡奏牘違戾法式者，貼說以進。

translations.literal: Memorials violating prescribed format were submitted with explanatory notes attached.
translations.idiomatic: Nonconforming memorials were submitted with explanatory notes attached.

sentences.zh: 熙寧四年，詔：“應朝廷擢用材能、賞功罰罪事可懲勸者，中書檢正、樞密院檢詳官月以事狀錄付院，謄報天下。”

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xining, an edict stated: "Matters in which the court promotes talent, rewards merit, and punishes wrongdoing that may serve as encouragement and warning—the Secretariat's verification officers and the Bureau of Military Affairs' review officers shall each month record the facts and send them to the office for copying and reporting throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Xining 4: an edict required that each month the Secretariat's verification officers and the Military Bureau's review officers record cases of talent promotion, rewards, and punishments suitable for public moral instruction and relay them to the Memorial Submission Office for copying and empire-wide distribution.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，罷之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era, it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The practice was abolished at the start of the Yuanyou reign.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，詔如熙寧舊條。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng, an edict restored the former Xining provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Shaosheng 1: an edict restored the Xining-era rules.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年二月，詔：“諸道監司、帥守文字，應邊防機密急切事，許進奏院直赴通進司投進。”

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Jingkang, an edict stated: "Documents from circuit intendants and military prefects concerning urgent frontier secrets may be submitted directly from the Memorial Submission Office to the Document Relay Office.
translations.idiomatic: Jingkang 1, second month: an edict allowed circuit supervisors and prefects' urgent frontier documents to be sent directly from the Memorial Submission Office to the Document Relay Office.

sentences.zh: 舊制，通進、銀台司，知司官二人，兩制以上充。

translations.literal: Under the old system, the Document Relay and Silver Terrace offices each had two supervising officials, filled by holders of two-edict posts and above.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly each of the Document Relay and Silver Terrace offices had two supervising officials drawn from the two-edict ranks and above.

sentences.zh: 通進司，掌受銀台司所領天下章奏案牘，及閣門在京百司奏牘、文武近臣表疏，以進御，然後頒佈於外。

translations.literal: The Document Relay Office received memorial files from throughout the realm managed by the Silver Terrace Office, together with memorials from all capital agencies submitted through the Gate Office and petitions from civil and military officials near the throne; it presented them to the emperor and then promulgated them outside.
translations.idiomatic: The Document Relay Office took in empire-wide memorial files from the Silver Terrace Office, capital-agency memorials routed through the Gate Office, and near-court officials' petitions, presented them to the throne, and then distributed copies beyond the palace.

sentences.zh: 銀台司，掌受天下奏狀案牘，抄錄其目進御，發付勾檢，糾其違失而督其淹綬。

translations.literal: The Silver Terrace Office received memorial petitions and files from throughout the realm, copied out item lists for presentation to the emperor, forwarded them for audit, corrected violations, and pressed against delay.
translations.idiomatic: The Silver Terrace Office received petitions and files from across the realm, logged itemized summaries for imperial review, sent them for audit, corrected irregularities, and enforced timely handling.

sentences.zh: 發敕司，掌受中書、樞密院宣敕，著籍以頒下之。

translations.literal: The Edict Dispatch Office received proclamations and orders from the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs, registered them, and issued them downward.
translations.idiomatic: The Edict Dispatch Office took proclamations and orders from the Secretariat and Military Bureau, entered them in the register, and distributed them downward.

sentences.zh: 登聞檢院，隸諫議大夫；

translations.literal: The Petition Review Office was subordinate to the Remonstrance Grandee;
translations.idiomatic: The Petition Review Office reported to the Remonstrance Grandee;

sentences.zh: 登聞鼓院，隸司諫、正言 掌受文武官及士民章奏表疏。

translations.literal: the Petition Drum Office was subordinate to the Remonstrance Bureau Director and Rectifier and received memorials and petitions from civil and military officials and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: the Petition Drum Office reported to the Remonstrance Bureau director and rectifier and received petitions from officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 凡言朝政得失、公私利害、軍期機密、陳乞恩賞、理雪冤濫，及奇方異術、改換文資、改正過名，無例通進者，先經鼓院進狀；

translations.literal: Whenever one wished to speak on the gains and losses of court policy, public and private interests, military deadlines and secrets, requests for favor and reward, redress of injustice and abuse, unusual remedies and arts, changes of document status, or correction of erroneous names, and there was no precedent for direct submission, one first filed at the Drum Office;
translations.idiomatic: Matters without precedent for direct submission—policy critique, public or private grievance, military secrets, petitions for reward, requests to clear injustice, unusual arts, changes of document status, or name corrections—had first to be filed at the Drum Office;

sentences.zh: 或為所抑，則詣檢院。

translations.literal: if blocked there, one then went to the Review Office.
translations.idiomatic: if turned away there, one could appeal to the Review Office.

sentences.zh: 並置局於關門之前。

translations.literal: Both offices maintained bureaus before the Gate of Passage.
translations.idiomatic: Both maintained desks before the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 中興後，檢、鼓、糧、審計、官告、進奏，謂之六院。

translations.literal: After the restoration, the Review, Drum, Grain, Audit, Commission, and Memorial Submission offices were called the Six Offices.
translations.idiomatic: After the Southern restoration, the Review, Drum, Grain, Audit, Commission, and Memorial Submission offices were collectively termed the Six Offices.

sentences.zh: 例以京官知縣有政績者充；

translations.literal: By precedent they were filled by capital officials who had served as magistrates with administrative merit;
translations.idiomatic: By custom they were staffed by capital officials who had distinguished themselves as county magistrates;

sentences.zh: 亦有自郡守除者，繼即除郎。

translations.literal: some were appointed from prefectural posts and were immediately promoted to court gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: some were drawn from prefectural posts and promptly promoted to court gentleman rank.

sentences.zh: 恩數略視職事官，而不入雜壓。

translations.literal: Their perquisites were broadly comparable to those of functional officials, but they were not entered in the mixed precedence roll.
translations.idiomatic: Their perquisites roughly matched those of functional officials, yet they were omitted from the mixed seniority roll.

sentences.zh: 紹興十一年，胡汝明以料院除監察御史，遂遷侍御史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shaoxing, Hu Ruming was appointed Remonstrance Censor from the Grain Office and was soon promoted to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 11: Hu Ruming moved from the Grain Office to Remonstrance Censor and soon rose to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 乾道後，相繼入台者數人，六院彌重，為察官之儲。

translations.literal: After the Qiandao era, several men in succession entered the Censorate; the Six Offices grew weightier and served as a reserve for investigating censors.
translations.idiomatic: After Qiandao, several appointees entered the Censorate in succession; the Six Offices gained standing as a training ground for investigating censors.

sentences.zh: 淳熙初，班寺監、丞之上。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunxi, they ranked above directors and vice-directors of the courts and directorates.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chunxi they were placed above directors and vice-directors of the courts and directorates.

sentences.zh: 紹熙二年，詔六院官復入雜壓，在九寺簿之下，六院各隨所隸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxi, an edict restored the Six Office officials to the mixed precedence roll, below registrars of the Nine Courts, each office according to its affiliation.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxi 2: an edict returned Six Office officials to the mixed roll, below Nine Courts registrars, ranked by each office's affiliation.

sentences.zh: 中書省 掌進擬庶務，宣奉命令，行台諫章疏、群臣奏請興創改革，及中外無法式事應取旨事。

translations.literal: Secretariat: it drafted routine business, promulgated commands, transmitted remonstrance memorials and petitions, and handled memorials and requests for new institutions and reforms, as well as matters within and without the court lacking statutory precedent that required imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat drafted routine business, issued commands, forwarded remonstrance memorials and officials' petitions, and handled proposals for new institutions and reforms and other matters lacking statutory precedent that required imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 凡除省、台、寺、監長貳以下，及侍從、職事官，外任監司、節鎮、知州、軍通判，武臣遙郡橫行以上除授，皆掌之。

translations.literal: It managed all appointments from deputy heads of the Three Departments, Censorate, courts, and directorates downward, attendant and functional officials, outer circuit intendants, military commissioners, prefects, military prefects and their vice-prefects, and remote military appointments from transverse commandant upward.
translations.idiomatic: It controlled appointments from deputy heads of the Three Departments, Censorate, courts, and directorates on down, attendant and functional officials, circuit intendants, commissioners, prefects and vice-prefects, and distant military posts from transverse commandant upward.

sentences.zh: 凡命令之體有七：曰冊書，立后妃，封親王、皇子、大長公主，拜三師、三公、三省長官，則用之。

translations.literal: There were seven forms of command: first, book of investiture—used when establishing empresses and consorts, enfeoffing imperial princes, princes, and grand princesses, or appointing the Three Preceptors, Three Excellencies, and chiefs of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Commands took seven forms. A book of investiture installed empresses and consorts, enfeoffed imperial princes and grand princesses, and appointed the Three Preceptors, Three Excellencies, and heads of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 曰制書，處分軍國大事，頒赦宥德音，命尚書左右僕射、開府儀同三司、節度使，凡告廷除授，則用之。

translations.literal: Second, edict of state—used when disposing of great military and state affairs, issuing amnesties and grace pronouncements, or appointing Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Preceptors with the Ceremonial Regalia of a Grand Duchy, and military commissioners, and for all court announcements of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of state addressed major military and civil affairs, proclaimed amnesties and grace edicts, and appointed vice directors, grand preceptors with ducal ceremonial honors, and military commissioners—in short, all formal court appointments.

sentences.zh: 曰誥命，應文武官遷改職秩、內外命婦除授及封敘、贈典，應合命詞，則用之。

translations.literal: Third, patent of appointment—used whenever civil and military officials changed rank, inner and outer titled ladies received appointment, enfeoffment, posthumous honors, or commemorative grants requiring formal wording.
translations.idiomatic: A patent of appointment covered civil and military promotions, appointments of titled ladies within and without the court, enfeoffments, posthumous honors, and other grants requiring formal wording.

sentences.zh: 曰詔書，賜待制、大卿監、中大夫、觀察使以上，則用之。

translations.literal: Fourth, edict of grace—used when bestowing posts from Hanlin Academician on Special Assignment upward, grand directors of courts and directorates, and Grandee of Palace Attendance and Observation Commissioner upward.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of grace was used for appointments from Hanlin Academician on Special Assignment upward, grand court and directorate directors, and grandees of palace attendance and observation commissioners upward.

sentences.zh: 曰敕書，賜少卿監、中散大夫、防禦使以下，則用之。

translations.literal: Fifth, edict of commission—used when bestowing posts from vice director of courts and directorates, Palace Attendant, and Defense Commissioner downward.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of commission applied to appointments from vice court and directorate directors, palace attendants, and defense commissioners downward.

sentences.zh: 曰御札，佈告登封、郊祀、宗祀及大號令，則用之。

translations.literal: Sixth, imperial note—used when proclaiming ascents to sacred peaks, suburban and ancestral sacrifices, and great proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial note announced mountaintop rites, suburban and ancestral sacrifices, and major proclamations.

sentences.zh: 曰敕榜，賜酺及戒勵百官、曉諭軍民，則用之。

translations.literal: Seventh, edict placard—used when granting public feasts and admonishing the hundred officials or instructing soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: An edict placard granted public feasts and admonished officials or instructed soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 皆承製畫旨以授門下省，令宣之，侍郎奉之，舍人行之。

translations.literal: All received drafted imperial decisions and were transmitted to the Chancellery for promulgation; the vice director received them and the drafter executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Each form received a drafted imperial decision, passed to the Chancellery for promulgation, was received by the vice director, and executed by the drafter.

sentences.zh: 留其所得旨為底：大事奏稟得旨者為“畫黃，

translations.literal: The decisions received were kept as master copies: for major affairs reported upward and approved, the record was called "marked yellow";
translations.idiomatic: Received decisions were filed as master copies: major matters reported upward and approved were recorded as "marked yellow";

sentences.zh: 小事擬進得旨者為 “錄黃”。

translations.literal: for minor affairs drafted for submission and approved, the record was called "record yellow."
translations.idiomatic: minor matters drafted for submission and approved were recorded as "record yellow."

sentences.zh: 凡事乾因革損益，而非法式所載者，論定而上之。

translations.literal: Whenever a matter involved innovation, reduction, or increase not covered by statute, it was deliberated and submitted upward.
translations.idiomatic: Any institutional change not covered by statute was deliberated and submitted for approval.

sentences.zh: 諸司傳宣、特旨，承報審覆，然後行下。

translations.literal: Special announcements and extraordinary orders from the agencies were received, reviewed, and only then issued downward.
translations.idiomatic: Agency announcements and special imperial orders were received, reviewed, and only then transmitted downward.

sentences.zh: 設官十有一：令、侍郎、右散騎常侍各一人，舍人四人，右諫議大夫、起居舍人、右司諫、右正言各一人。

translations.literal: There were eleven posts: one director, one vice director, one Right Regular Attendant of the Imperial Horse, four drafters, and one each of Right Remonstrance Grandee, Diarist, Right Remonstrance Bureau Director, and Right Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven posts were established: director, vice director, Right Regular Attendant of the Imperial Horse, four drafters, and one each of Right Remonstrance Grandee, diarist, Right Remonstrance Bureau director, and Right rectifier.

sentences.zh: 分房八、曰吏房，曰戶房，曰兵禮房，曰刑房，曰工房，曰主事房，曰班簿房，曰制敕庫房。

translations.literal: There were eight sections: Personnel, Revenue, Military-Rites, Punishments, Works, Correspondence, Roster, and Edict Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Eight sections handled the work: Personnel, Revenue, Military-Rites, Punishments, Works, Correspondence, Roster, and Edict Archive.

sentences.zh: 元祐以後，析兵、禮為二，增催驅、點檢，分房十有一，後又改主事房為開拆。

translations.literal: After Yuanyou, Military-Rites was split in two, Expediting and Inspection were added, making eleven sections; later the Correspondence Section was renamed Opening and Sorting.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanyou, Military-Rites was divided, Expediting and Inspection were added for eleven sections total; later Correspondence was renamed Opening and Sorting.

sentences.zh: 凡吏房，掌行除授、考察、升黜、賞罰、廢置、薦舉、假故、一時差官文書。

translations.literal: The Personnel Section handled documents for appointments, evaluations, promotion and demotion, rewards and punishments, abolition and establishment of posts, recommendations, leave, and temporary assignments.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel processed appointments, evaluations, promotions and demotions, rewards and punishments, abolitions and creations of posts, recommendations, leave, and temporary assignments.

sentences.zh: 曰戶房，掌行廢置升降郡縣、調發邊防軍須、給貸錢物。

translations.literal: The Revenue Section handled abolition, establishment, promotion, and demotion of commanderies and counties, frontier military supplies, and loans of money and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue handled changes to counties and prefectures, frontier military supplies, and loans of money and goods.

sentences.zh: 曰禮房，掌行郊祀陵廟典禮、后妃皇子公主大臣封冊、科舉考官、外夷書詔。

translations.literal: The Rites Section handled suburban and ancestral rites, enfeoffment of empresses, princes, princesses, and great ministers, examination officials, and letters and edicts to foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: Rites handled suburban and ancestral ceremonies, enfeoffments of the imperial family and great ministers, examination officials, and diplomatic correspondence.

sentences.zh: 曰兵房，掌行除授諸蕃國王爵、官封。

translations.literal: The Military Section handled enfeoffment of foreign kings and bestowal of titles.
translations.idiomatic: Military handled enfeoffments of foreign kings and the granting of titles.

sentences.zh: 曰刑房，掌行赦宥及貶降、敘復。

translations.literal: The Punishments Section handled amnesties and demotions, restorations, and reinstatements.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments handled amnesties, demotions, restorations, and reinstatements.

sentences.zh: 曰工房，掌行營造計度及河防修閉。

translations.literal: The Works Section handled construction estimates and river-control repair and closure.
translations.idiomatic: Works handled construction estimates and river-control projects.

sentences.zh: 凡尚書省所上奏請、台諫所陳章疏、內外臣僚官司申請無法式應取旨者，六房各視其名而行之。

translations.literal: Whenever the Department of State Affairs submitted memorials, the Censorate submitted remonstrance memorials, or inner and outer officials and agencies applied on matters lacking statutory precedent requiring imperial decision, each of the six sections handled them according to subject.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials from the Department of State Affairs, remonstrance submissions from the Censorate, and applications from officials and agencies on matters without statutory precedent were routed to the six sections by subject.

sentences.zh: 曰主事房，掌行受發文書。

translations.literal: The Correspondence Section handled receipt and dispatch of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Correspondence received and dispatched documents.

sentences.zh: 曰班簿房，掌百官名籍具員。

translations.literal: The Roster Section maintained the full roster of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Roster maintained the complete register of officials and authorized posts.

sentences.zh: 曰制敕庫房，掌編錄供檢敕、令、格、式及架閣庫。

translations.literal: The Edict Archive Section compiled edicts, orders, regulations, and forms for reference and maintained the archive storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Edict Archive compiled edicts, orders, regulations, and forms for reference and maintained the archive.

sentences.zh: 曰催驅房，督趣稽違。

translations.literal: The Expediting Section pressed against delay and violation.
translations.idiomatic: Expediting enforced deadlines and corrected delays.

sentences.zh: 曰點檢房，省察差失。

translations.literal: The Inspection Section examined errors and omissions.
translations.idiomatic: Inspection reviewed errors and omissions.

sentences.zh: 吏四十有五：錄事三人，主事四人，令史七人，書令史十有四人，守當官十有七人。

translations.literal: There were forty-five clerks: three recorders, four chief clerks, seven clerks, fourteen writing clerks, and seventeen duty clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-five clerks served: three recorders, four chief clerks, seven clerks, fourteen writing clerks, and seventeen duty clerks.

sentences.zh: 而外省吏十有九人：令史一人，書令史二人，守當官六人，守闕守當官 十人。

translations.literal: Outside the capital there were nineteen clerks: one clerk, two writing clerks, six duty clerks, and ten reserve duty clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the capital nineteen clerks were assigned: one clerk, two writing clerks, six duty clerks, and ten reserve duty clerks.

sentences.zh: 元豐八年，詔待制以上磨勘，本省進擬。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanfeng, an edict ordered that merit reviews for Academician on Special Assignment and above be drafted by this department.
translations.idiomatic: the eighth year of Yuanfeng: merit reviews for Academician on Special Assignment and above were to be drafted by the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元祐三年，詔應除授從中批付中書省者，並三省行。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanyou, an edict ordered that appointments marked for the Secretariat in the inner draft were all processed through the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou 3: appointments marked in the inner draft for the Secretariat were routed through all Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 紹聖五年，詔臣僚上殿扎子，中書省進呈取旨；

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaosheng, an edict ordered that when officials submitted folded memorials at audience, the Secretariat was to present them for imperial decision;
translations.idiomatic: Shaosheng 5: folded audience memorials from officials were to be presented by the Secretariat for imperial decision;

sentences.zh: 其承受傳宣、內降，非有司所可行者，申中書省或樞密院奏審。

translations.literal: when receiving special announcements or inner orders that the responsible agencies could not execute, one was to report to the Secretariat or Bureau of Military Affairs for memorial review.
translations.idiomatic: special announcements and inner orders that responsible agencies could not execute were to be reported to the Secretariat or Military Bureau for review.

sentences.zh: 令掌佐天子議大政，授所行命令而宣之。

translations.literal: The director assisted the Son of Heaven in deliberating great affairs, received the commands to be executed, and promulgated them.
translations.idiomatic: The director assisted the emperor in deliberating major policy, received commands for execution, and promulgated them.

sentences.zh: 祀大神祇則升壇，享宗廟則升阼階而相其禮。

translations.literal: When sacrificing to the great spirits he ascended the altar; when offering in the ancestral temple he ascended the eastern steps and assisted in the rites.
translations.idiomatic: At sacrifices to the great spirits he ascended the altar; at ancestral offerings he mounted the eastern steps and directed the rites.

sentences.zh: 臨軒冊命則讀冊。

translations.literal: At investiture before the throne he read the book of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At throne-side investiture he read the book of appointment.

sentences.zh: 建儲則升殿宣制，持冊及璽綬以授太子。

translations.literal: When establishing an heir he ascended the hall to proclaim the edict, holding the book and seal-cord to invest the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When installing an heir he ascended the hall to proclaim the edict and presented the book and seal-cord to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 大朝會則詣御坐前奏方鎮表及祥瑞。

translations.literal: At great court assemblies he went before the imperial seat to present frontier memorials and auspicious reports.
translations.idiomatic: At great court assemblies he presented frontier memorials and reports of auspicious omens before the throne.

sentences.zh: 國朝未嘗真拜，以他官兼領者不預政事，然止曹佾一人，餘皆贈官。

translations.literal: In our dynasty the post was never truly conferred; of those who held it concurrently by another office and did not participate in governance, only Cao You was one person—the rest were posthumous appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The Song never truly filled the post; of those who held it concurrently without joining governance, only Cao You was a living appointee—the rest were posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 官制行，以右僕射兼中書侍郎行令之職，別置侍郎以佐之。

translations.literal: When the office system took effect, the Right Vice Director concurrently served as Secretariat Vice Director performing the director's duties, and a separate vice director was established to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Under the office reform the Right Vice Director doubled as Secretariat vice director performing the director's duties, with a separate vice director to assist.

sentences.zh: 中興後，置左、右丞相，省令不置。

translations.literal: After the restoration, Left and Right Chancellors were established and the Secretariat director was not filled.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration Left and Right Chancellors were installed and the Secretariat directorship was left vacant.

sentences.zh: 侍郎 掌貳令之職，參議大政，授所宣詔旨而奉之。

translations.literal: Vice Director: he shared the director's duties, deliberated great affairs, received proclamations and edicts to be promulgated, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: The vice director shared the director's duties, deliberated major policy, received proclamations and edicts for promulgation, and presented them.

sentences.zh: 凡大朝會則押表及祥瑞案。

translations.literal: At great court assemblies he held the memorials and the file of auspicious reports.
translations.idiomatic: At great court assemblies he held memorials and the file of auspicious reports.

sentences.zh: 臨軒冊命則押冊引案，以所奏文及冊書授令。

translations.literal: At throne-side investiture he held the book and led the file, presenting the memorial text and book of appointment to the director.
translations.idiomatic: At throne-side investiture he held the book, led the file forward, and handed the memorial text and book of appointment to the director.

sentences.zh: 四夷來朝則奏其表疏，以贄幣付有司。

translations.literal: When the four barbarians came to court he presented their memorials and turned tribute goods over to the responsible agency.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign envoys came to court he presented their memorials and delivered tribute goods to the responsible agency.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，復置參知政事，省中書侍郎不置。

translations.literal: After the southward move, Vice Grand Councillors were restored and the Secretariat vice director was not filled.
translations.idiomatic: After the move south Vice Grand Councillors were restored and the Secretariat vice directorship was abolished.

sentences.zh: 舍人四人，舊六人。

translations.literal: There were four drafters; formerly six.
translations.idiomatic: Four drafters were authorized; formerly there had been six.

sentences.zh: 掌行命令為制詞，分治六房，隨房當制，事有失當及除授非其人，則論奏封還詞頭。

translations.literal: They drafted command wording, divided responsibility among the six sections, and drafted according to section; when matters were improper or appointments unsuitable, they memorialized and returned the draft head.
translations.idiomatic: They drafted command texts, were assigned to the six sections, and drafted by rotation; when a matter or appointment was improper they memorialized and returned the draft.

sentences.zh: 國初，為所遷官，實不任職，復置知制誥及直舍人院，主行詞命，與學士對掌內外製。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty the post was a nominal promotion without real duties; the Drafting Academician and Direct Drafting Office were restored to handle wording, pairing with the Hanlin Academician in inner and outer drafting.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty the post was a nominal promotion without real duties; Drafting Academician and the Direct Drafting Office were restored to handle wording, pairing with the Hanlin Academician for inner and outer drafts.

sentences.zh: 凡有除拜，中書吏赴院納詞頭。

translations.literal: Whenever there was an appointment, Secretariat clerks went to the office to submit the draft head.
translations.idiomatic: For each appointment Secretariat clerks delivered the draft head to the drafting office.

sentences.zh: 其大除拜，亦有宰相召舍人面授詞頭者。

translations.literal: For major appointments, the chief minister sometimes summoned a drafter and orally conveyed the draft head.
translations.idiomatic: For major appointments the chief minister sometimes summoned a drafter and conveyed the draft head in person.

sentences.zh: 若大誥命，中書並敕進入，從中而下，餘則發敕官受而出之。

translations.literal: For great patents of appointment, the Secretariat submitted the draft together with the order and it descended from the inner court; for the rest, the edict-dispatch officer received and issued them.
translations.idiomatic: Great patents of appointment were submitted together with the order from the inner court; lesser appointments were issued by the edict-dispatch officer.

sentences.zh: 及修官制，遂以實正名，而判後省之事。

translations.literal: When the office system was revised, the post received its true title and adjudicated affairs of the rear department.
translations.idiomatic: When the offices were reformed the post became a substantive appointment with authority over the rear department.

sentences.zh: 分案五：曰上案，掌冊禮及朝會所行事；

translations.literal: There were five desks: Upper, handling book rites and court-assembly duties;
translations.idiomatic: Five desks were established: Upper, for book rites and court-assembly duties;

sentences.zh: 曰下案，掌受付文書；

translations.literal: Lower, handling receipt and dispatch of documents;
translations.idiomatic: Lower, for receipt and dispatch of documents;

sentences.zh: 曰制誥案，掌書錄製詞及試吏，校其功過；

translations.literal: Drafting, recording draft texts and testing clerks and reviewing their merit and fault;
translations.idiomatic: Drafting, for recording draft texts, testing clerks, and reviewing their performance;

sentences.zh: 曰諫官案，掌受諸司關報文書；

translations.literal: Remonstrance, receiving notification documents from the agencies;
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance, for receiving notification documents from agencies;

sentences.zh: 曰記註案，掌錄記註。

translations.literal: Record, keeping the court diary.
translations.idiomatic: Record, for maintaining the court diary.

sentences.zh: 其雜務則隨所分案掌之。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous duties were handled according to the assigned desk.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous duties fell to whichever desk was assigned.

sentences.zh: 元豐六年，詔中書省置點檢房，令舍人通領。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng, an edict established an Inspection Section in the Secretariat, jointly supervised by the director and drafters.
translations.idiomatic: the sixth year of Yuanfeng: an Inspection Section was established in the Secretariat under joint supervision of the director and drafters.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，詔舍人各簽諸房文字，其命詞則輪日分草。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, an edict ordered each drafter to countersign documents of the various sections; for command wording they drafted in daily rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou 1: each drafter was to countersign section documents; command wording rotated daily among them.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔時暫闕官，依門下、尚書省例，送本省官兼權。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict ordered that when posts were temporarily vacant, following the precedent of the Chancellery and Department of State Affairs, an official of this department should serve concurrently on provisional assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: when posts were temporarily vacant, following Chancellery and Department precedent, a Secretariat official was to serve on provisional assignment.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年，蹇序辰請自今命詞，以元行遣文書同檢送當制舍人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaosheng, Jian Xuchen requested that henceforth for command wording the original dispatch document be jointly submitted to the drafter on duty.
translations.idiomatic: Shaosheng 4: Jian Xuchen asked that command drafts hereafter be checked against the original dispatch document by the drafter on duty.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 建炎後同，他官兼攝者則稱權舍人，資淺者為直舍人院。

translations.literal: After the Jianyan era it was the same; when another official served concurrently he was styled Acting Drafter, and the less senior served in the Direct Drafting Office.
translations.idiomatic: After Jianyan the practice continued; concurrent appointees were styled Acting Drafter, with junior officials serving in the Direct Drafting Office.

sentences.zh: 起居舍人一人，掌同門下省起居郎。

translations.literal: One Diarist, sharing the duties of the Chancellery Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: One diarist shared the duties of the Chancellery diarist.

sentences.zh: 侍立修註官，元豐前，以起居郎、舍人寄祿，而更命他官領其事，謂之同修起居註。

translations.literal: Attendant recorders: before Yuanfeng, the Diarist and Drafter held salary posts while another official was appointed to the duty, styled Co-recorder of the Court Diary.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant recorders: before Yuanfeng the diarist and drafter held salary posts while another official performed the duty as Co-recorder of the Court Diary.

sentences.zh: 官制行，以郎、舍人為職任。

translations.literal: When the office system took effect, the gentleman and drafter became the substantive appointees.
translations.idiomatic: Under the office reform the gentleman and drafter became substantive appointees.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十五年，羅點自戶部員外郎為起居舍人，避其祖諱，乃以為太常少卿兼侍立修註官。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Chunxi, Luo Dian was appointed Diarist from Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue; to avoid his grandfather's tabooed name he was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices concurrently serving as attendant recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 15: Luo Dian was promoted from Vice Director of Revenue to diarist; to avoid his grandfather's tabooed name he was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with concurrent duty as attendant recorder.

sentences.zh: 其後兩史或闕而用資淺者，則降旨以某人權侍立修註官。

translations.literal: Thereafter when either diarist was vacant and a junior official was used, an edict appointed someone to serve provisionally as attendant recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter when a diarist post was vacant a junior official might be appointed by edict to serve provisionally as attendant recorder.

sentences.zh: 右散騎常侍 右諫議大夫 右司諫 右正言與門下省同，但左屬門下，右屬中書，皆附兩省班籍，通謂之兩省官。

translations.literal: Right Regular Attendant of the Imperial Horse, Right Remonstrance Grandee, Right Remonstrance Bureau Director, and Right Rectifier were the same as in the Chancellery, but the left belonged to the Chancellery and the right to the Secretariat; both were attached to the two departments' roster and were collectively called Two-Department officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Regular Attendant, Right Remonstrance Grandee, Right Remonstrance Bureau director, and Right rectifier mirrored their Chancellery counterparts; the left posts belonged to the Chancellery and the right to the Secretariat. Both sets were on the two departments' roster and were collectively termed Two-Department officials.

sentences.zh: 元豐既新官制，職事官未有不經除授者，惟御史大夫、左右散騎常侍，始終未嘗一除人。

translations.literal: After Yuanfeng's new office system, no functional post went unfilled by appointment except Censor-in-Chief and Left and Right Regular Attendants of the Imperial Horse—neither was ever once filled.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanfeng's reform every functional post received an appointee except Censor-in-Chief and the Left and Right Regular Attendants—neither was ever filled.

sentences.zh: 蓋兩官為台諫之長，無有啟之者。

translations.literal: This was because the two posts were heads of the Censorate and Remonstrance Bureau, and no one initiated appointment to them.
translations.idiomatic: Both were heads of the Censorate and Remonstrance Bureau, and no one ever proposed filling them.

sentences.zh: 中興初，詔諫院不隸兩省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the restoration, an edict removed the Remonstrance Bureau from subordination to the Two Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the restoration an edict detached the Remonstrance Bureau from the Two Departments.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，詔並依舊赴三省元置局處。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, an edict ordered that they again attend at the original bureaus of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 2: an edict restored attendance at the Three Departments' original bureau sites.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十五年，用林慄言，置左右補闕、拾遺，專任諫正，不任糾劾之事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Chunxi, following Lin Li's proposal, Left and Right Omission and Reminder posts were established, charged solely with remonstrance and correction and not with impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi 15: following Lin Li's proposal, Left and Right Omission and Reminder posts were created for remonstrance alone, without impeachment duties.

sentences.zh: 逾年減罷。

translations.literal: After more than a year they were reduced and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year they were abolished.

sentences.zh: 法司令史、書令史、守當官各一人，守闕守當官三人，乾道六年減二人。

translations.literal: For the law section there were one clerk, one document clerk, and one duty officer each; three reserve duty officers; in the sixth year of Qiandao two posts were cut.
translations.idiomatic: The law section had one clerk, one document clerk, and one duty officer apiece, plus three reserve duty officers; two posts were eliminated in Qiandao 6.

sentences.zh: 檢正官五房各一人，掌糾正省務。

translations.literal: Rectification officials numbered one for each of the five sections, managing correction of department business.
translations.idiomatic: One rectification official was assigned to each of the five sections to oversee correction of departmental affairs.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年置，以京朝官充，選人即為習學公事。

translations.literal: Established in the third year of Xining; capital officials filled the posts, and selected candidates served as probationary clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The office was created in Xining 3, staffed by capital officials; examination graduates entered as probationary clerks.

sentences.zh: 官制行，罷之，而其職歸左右司。

translations.literal: When the new offices took effect they were abolished, and their duties passed to the Left and Right Secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: Under the office reform the posts were abolished and their duties transferred to the Left and Right Secretariats.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，中書門下省言：“軍興以來，天下多事，中書別無屬官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan the Chancellery-Secretariat reported: "Since military campaigns began, affairs throughout the realm have multiplied, and the Secretariat has no subordinate officials of its own.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 3 the Chancellery-Secretariat reported: "Since the outbreak of war, business throughout the empire has multiplied, yet the Secretariat has no dedicated subordinate staff.

sentences.zh: 元豐以前，有檢正官，後因置左右司，遂不差，致朝廷及應報四方行移稽留，無檢舉催促。

translations.literal: Before Yuanfeng there were rectification officials; afterward, with the establishment of the Left and Right Secretariats, none were assigned, so court business and outgoing documents to the four quarters lagged without inspection or urging.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yuanfeng rectification officials had existed; once the Left and Right Secretariats were established, however, none were appointed, and court business and outgoing documents to the provinces piled up without review or follow-up.

sentences.zh: 今欲差官兩員充中書門下省檢正諸房公事。

translations.literal: It is now proposed to assign two officials as rectification clerks for all sections of the Chancellery-Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was to appoint two officials as rectification clerks for all sections of the Chancellery-Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 內一員檢正吏、禮、兵房，一員檢正戶、刑、工房。

translations.literal: Of these, one would rectify the Personnel, Rites, and Military sections, and one the Revenue, Justice, and Works sections.
translations.idiomatic: One would oversee the Personnel, Rites, and Military sections; the other the Revenue, Justice, and Works sections.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 至次年，詔並罷。

translations.literal: The following year an edict abolished them all.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict abolished the posts entirely.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，詔中書門下省復置檢正官一員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing an edict restored one rectification official for the Chancellery-Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 2 an edict restored a single rectification official for the Chancellery-Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年指揮，中書門下省併為一。

translations.literal: Under the directive of the third year of Jianyan the Chancellery and Secretariat were merged into one.
translations.idiomatic: Per the Jianyan 3 directive, the Chancellery and Secretariat were combined into a single department.

sentences.zh: 中書省錄事、主事、令史、書令史、守當官共四十三人；

translations.literal: For the Secretariat there were forty-three record clerks, chief clerks, clerks, document clerks, and duty officers in all;
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat had forty-three record clerks, chief clerks, clerks, document clerks, and duty officers combined;

sentences.zh: 門下省錄事、主事、令史、書令史、守當官共四十六人，依祖額以八十九人為額。

translations.literal: for the Chancellery, forty-six in the same categories; per the original quota the authorized total was eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: the Chancellery had forty-six in the same categories; under the original quota the authorized total was eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 守闕守當官兩省各一百人，共存留一百五十人，中書省六分，門下省四分。

translations.literal: Each of the two departments had one hundred reserve duty officers; one hundred fifty were retained in all, apportioned six parts to the Secretariat and four to the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Each department had one hundred reserve duty officers on the rolls; one hundred fifty were retained in all, allocated sixty percent to the Secretariat and forty percent to the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 尚書省掌施行制命，舉省內綱紀程式，受付六曹文書，聽內外辭訴，奏御史失職，考百官庶府之治否，以詔廢置、賞罰。

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs managed the execution of issued orders, upheld the department's regulations and procedures, received and dispatched documents of the Six Ministries, heard petitions from within and without, memorialized on censorial dereliction, and assessed whether officials and agencies performed their duties, reporting to the throne for abolition, appointment, reward, and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs executed issued orders, maintained internal regulations and procedures, received and routed Six Ministries documents, heard internal and external petitions, reported censorial failures, and evaluated the performance of officials and agencies, recommending appointments, dismissals, rewards, and punishments to the throne.

sentences.zh: 曰吏部，曰戶部，曰禮部，曰兵部，曰刑部，曰工部，皆隸焉。

translations.literal: There were the Ministry of Personnel, Ministry of Revenue, Ministry of Rites, Ministry of War, Ministry of Justice, and Ministry of Works — all subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel, Revenue, Rites, War, Justice, and Works all fell under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 凡天下之務，六曹所不能與奪者，總決之；

translations.literal: Affairs throughout the realm that the Six Ministries could neither grant nor withhold it decided in the aggregate;
translations.idiomatic: Matters empire-wide that the Six Ministries could neither approve nor deny were decided at this level;

sentences.zh: 應取裁者，隨所隸送中書省、樞密院。

translations.literal: those requiring imperial decision were forwarded according to jurisdiction to the Secretariat or Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: cases requiring imperial decision were forwarded to the Secretariat or Bureau of Military Affairs according to jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 事有成法，則六曹準式具鈔，令、僕射、丞檢察簽書，送門下省畫聞。

translations.literal: When established precedent existed, the Six Ministries prepared copies per regulation; the Minister, Vice Directors, and Vice Commissioners inspected, signed, and sent them to the Chancellery for notation.
translations.idiomatic: Where precedent applied, the Six Ministries prepared regulated copies; the Minister, Vice Directors, and Vice Commissioners reviewed, signed, and forwarded them to the Chancellery for notation.

sentences.zh: 審察吏部註擬文武官及封爵承襲、賜勛定賞之事。

translations.literal: It scrutinized the Ministry of Personnel's nominations of civil and military officials and matters of enfeoffment, succession to titles, bestowal of honors, and fixed rewards.
translations.idiomatic: It reviewed Ministry of Personnel nominations for civil and military posts and matters of enfeoffment, title succession, honors, and fixed rewards.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有疑事，則集百官議其可否。

translations.literal: When the court had doubtful matters, it convened all officials to debate their propriety.
translations.idiomatic: When the court faced doubtful matters, it convened officials to debate their propriety.

sentences.zh: 凡更改申明敕令格式、一司條法，則議定以奏覆，太常、考功謚議亦如之。

translations.literal: For revisions and clarifications of edicts, formats, and single-agency regulations, it deliberated and memorialized for approval; posthumous titles and merit evaluations followed the same procedure.
translations.idiomatic: Revisions and clarifications of edicts, formats, and single-agency regulations were deliberated and submitted for approval; posthumous titles and merit evaluations followed the same process.

sentences.zh: 季終，具賞罰勸懲事付進奏院，頒行於天下。

translations.literal: At each quarter's end it compiled records of rewards, punishments, encouragement, and admonition and delivered them to the Memorial Submission Office for promulgation throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At quarter's end it compiled records of rewards, punishments, encouragement, and admonition and sent them to the Memorial Submission Office for empire-wide promulgation.

sentences.zh: 大祭祀則誓戒執事官。

translations.literal: At great sacrifices it administered the oath of abstinence to officiating officials.
translations.idiomatic: At major sacrifices it administered the abstinence oath to officiating officials.

sentences.zh: 令掌佐天子議大政，奉所出命令而行之。

translations.literal: The Minister assisted the Son of Heaven in deliberating great affairs of state and executed the orders issued from court.
